that this scheme of the Department will become functional during the current fiscal.

16
NATIONAL WELFARE FUNDS FOR SPORTS PERSONS
65. The Committee notes that the non plan fund amounting to `1 crore is allocated in BE
2015-16 for this scheme. During the BE as well as RE of 2014-15, the fund allocation was same,
i.e., for `1 crore. The Committee came to know that the National Welfare Fund for sportspersons
was set up in March, 1982 with a view to assisting outstanding sportspersons of the past, living in
indigent circumstances, who had brought glory for the country in sports. The Scheme has been
reviewed in July, 2009 to provide for lump sum ex-gratia assistance to outstanding sportspersons.
The provision of pension under this Scheme has been done away with as there is already a Scheme
of Pension for Meritorious Sportspersons. Now, a lump sum ex-gratia assistance is given to the
sportspersons or their families for medical treatment and for those living in indigent circumstances.
During 2014-15, financial assistance worth Rs. 82 lakh was sanctioned from National Welfare Fund
for Sportspersons . The Committee feels that this Scheme is a novel scheme but the allocation
of `1 crore appears to be ridiculous in view of the large number of eminent sportspersons,
having brought laurels to the country, are languishing in penury selling tea, vegetables, etc.
in the street. This is highly unbecoming to their status as well as to the country’s prestige.
This also demotivates our budding sportspersons and their parents to allow their children to
take up sports. Therefore, the Committee is of the considered opinion that all possible help
should be extended to our eminent former sportspersons in all possible manner and the
allocation should be increased at least ten times to begin with.
CONCLUSION
66. The execution of a mega sporting event helps in developing infrastructure, generating
employment, securing inflow of foreign capital and thus contributes significantly to the economic
development of a country. Therefore, if can be said that the impact of sports on the society is
multi-dimensional.
65. Despite varied and concerted efforts, the performance of Indian sports at the International
level is not very convincing. Therefore, a few steps may be recommended to make these initiatives
more comprehensive, like
➢ The allocation of funds, as the percentage of budget, should be increased rationally to
broad-base sports in the country.
➢ Sports should be made as an integral part of the education system to inculcate sports
culture from the school level.
➢ The effectiveness of the developmental projects should be evaluated periodically.
➢ Uniformity should be maintained in sports specific activities of various States of India
to provide equal participation opportunity to its citizens.
➢ A structure of good management, control and exercise should be incorporated to make
the system transparent and accountable.
66. The Committee feels that to revive sports culture, the Government should revisit the
sporting framework of India. This is also the need of the hour as India is reaping benefits
of demographic dividend in the form of young population which can easily be channelized
to sports and games for achieving better results. Otherwise, achievement of goals by
utilizing the available immense potential of the country in sports would be difficult to
realize. For achieving improved performance in sports internationally the government needs
to play a proactive role in promoting sports in India to establish the country as a sporting
nation. The Committee hopes that with improved sporting infrastructure and infusion of
latest technology in training of sportpersons India would show better results at the next
Olympics to be held at Rio in Brazil.

17
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE — AT A GLANCE
BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
The Committee notes with concern that there has been a gap between the projected
demands and the actual allocated funds during all these years. The Committee, therefore,
keeping in view the major emphasis of the Department during 2015-16 for preparation of
sports persons and teams for Rio Olympics 2016 feels that the Department should
endeavour to get enhancement of the fund at the RE stage so that the gap in allocation is
set off appropriately. The Committee also recommends that Ministry of Finance should
release more funds for the Department so that lack of funds should not come in the way
of our preparation as well as performance at the next Olympics and initiatives to be taken
by the Department also to tap non-governmental sources. (Para 11)
In view of the winding up of the Planning Commission, which was an in intermediary
agency between the Centre and the States, and also acted as monitoring agency, it is not
clear what monitoring mechanism of the centrally sponsored or central sector schemes
would be put in place. The Committee shows its concern and desires the Department to
clarify this issue before it at the earliest. (Para 12)
SPORTS AUTHORITY OF  INDIA (SAI)
The Committee notes that although of late there has been slight improvement in the
performance of India’s sportspersons at international events but it is incomparable with the
performance of other developing/developed nations for which a lot needs to be done. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that SAI should come up with more concerted efforts
so as to increase its medals tally substantially during Olympic Games, 2016. Improvement
of nation’s performance in sports is the need of the time as it would not only bring national
pride and glory but also instills some of confidence amongst the people. (Para 17)
The Committee notes with concern the reduced allocation for the SAI as compared
to BE of the last year. SAI is the agency mainly responsible for maintaining and
development of sports in the country. Reducing its allocation instead of increasing over the
years does not augur well for the development of sports in our country. (Para 19)
The Committee recommends that initiatives should be taken to fill up vacant posts
of Coaches urgently, required for every sports discipline and they get international training
and exposure regularly. The need for various levels of Coaches Education and Certification
System (CECS) structure, procedure for getting International Federations-Certification, etc.
have to be adequately taken care of besides the initiatives required for filling up the
vacancy of Coaches at the earliest. The existence of large-scale vacancies in respect of
Coaches should be serious cause for concern and the Committee fails to understand as to
how we are preparing our sportspersons in the absence of Coaches to compete with the
other nations at international sports events. (Para 20)
The Committee was given to understand that in Andhra Pradesh there is no dearth
of sports talents in archery, particularly in interior tribal areas. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that if the Budget allocation gets enhanced at the RE stage, the Department
may consider developing an archery training centre for Andhra Pradesh so as to tap the
17

18
potential of exemplary talents that have been lying in the rural tribal areas who would
contribute to the national sports talent. (Para 21)
ASSISTANCE TO NATIONAL SPORTS FEDERATIONS
The Committee, therefore, is of the opinion that there is a distinct lack of proper
coordination and control mechanism among the NSFs on the one hand, between, the
Ministry/SAI and the NSFs on the other hand. The NSFs in the name of their autonomy,
the Committee feels, that they are not accountable to anybody even though they receive
Government funds for their activities. The NSFs, the Committee, feels have a definite role
to play in promoting different sports disciplines in the country. But their working leaves
much to be desired. These bodies, unfortunately, devote much of their time and resources
in the non-sporting activities. Most of them have not been able to live upto the
expectations. No doubt, some of them done or doing very good work in the promotion of
sports in the country. The Committee has been expressing its concern over this issue from
time to time and calls upon the Ministry and the representatives of the NSFs to find out
collectively a most efficient and workable solution that can bring our sports sector out of
the present situations. We may perhaps try to learn/adopt the best practices in this respect
from the other countries such as China, Korea, Taiwan, etc. (Para 25)
The Committee finds it very disheartening on the issue of non-compliance of the
guidelines of the Department by the NSFs and recommends to evolve a suitable mechanism
in this regard so that the preparation as well as participation of the sportspersons in
important national and international events is not affected adversely. (Para 27)
AUDIT PARAS
The Committee is at a loss to see that the audit observations made in the
Commonwealth Games, 2010 by the CAG have not been cleared so far. The Committee finds
it objectionable and desires the Department to get this process completed at the very
earliest. (Para 28)
LAKSHMIBAI NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF PHYSICAL EDUCATION (LNIPE)
Presently, LNIPE has 863 students. The Committee came to know that the
Plan allocation amounting to `40 crores stagnated during the BE 2014-15 and also at RE
2014-15. However, it has increased to `45 crores in BE 2015-16. The Committee has noted
that a normal increase in BE 2015-16 is to meet establishment expenditure. The Committee
notes that the budget allocations have been sufficiently utilized but feels that the allocations
will not be enough for meeting the projected activities and requirement of the Institute
such as laying of squash court, tennis court, gymnasium, swimming pool, astro turf, boys
hostels, girls hostels, etc. The Committee, therefore, recommends for the enhanced budget
allocation to accomplish the proposed activities/works within the stipulated time frame.
(Para 30)
SPECIAL CASH AWARDS
The Committee while appreciating the enhanced allocation for cash awards for
sportspersons hopes that the enhanced allocation made during the BE 2015-16 would be fully
utilized to encourage and motivate outstanding sportspersons for higher achievements and
all backlogs are cleared in this regard. The Committee also observes that complete
transparency should be maintained while giving cash awards and that the criteria be
followed strictly in this regard. (Para 32)

19
URBAN SPORTS INFRASTRUCTURE
The Committee came to know that `40 crores was allocated for the purpose in BE
2014-15 and it was reduced to `25 crores in RE 2014-15. The Committee shows its concern
that the reduction in RE was on account of non-receipt of Utilisation Certificates by the
implementing agencies. The actual expenditure is amounting to `23.14 crores till February
2015. The Committee finds this as a very good scheme which is for providing sports
infrastructure in urban areas. But the allocation and expenditure pattern in respect of this
Scheme has been very discouraging. `40 crores BE is reduced to `25 crores RE and even
that could not be utilized fully. It was perhaps on account of such a poor pattern that the
allocation for BE 2015-16 has also been reduced to `25 crores. The Committee, accordingly
recommends that Department should take initiatives to expedite the submission of
utilization certificates by the implementing agencies in time so that the allocation pattern
is not affected adversely in future. (Para 35)
RAJIV GANDHI KHEL ABHIYAN (RGKA)
The Committee appreciates the launching of RGKA a centrally sponsored scheme in
place of earlier PYKKA scheme for its novel objectives of expanding and developing sports
specifically in the rural areas. This is a major Scheme to provide sports complexes for both
outdoor and I indoor disciplines in all the 6545 blocks 634 districts in phased manner over
a period of five years. Out in view of such humongous objectives of the scheme, the
performance both physical and financial during the last year does not inspire any confidence
that we will be able to achieve the objectives within the five years. The problem of pending
UCs should not be taken as an excuse in implementing such a flagship scheme.
(Para 41)
This Scheme has to work in convergence with different other schemes implemented by
different Ministries, the Committee feels that there may be possibility of lack of adequate co-
ordination and synergy in pooling the resources and the efforts for implementing this Scheme
effectively. The Committee, therefore, is of the view that a coordination mechanism especially
for this scheme should be put in place to obviate any such possibility. (Para 42)
Thirdly, the Committee is intrigued to note that `200 crore in the Plan allocation for
RGKA during BE 2014-15 was reduced to `85 crores in RE and even the reduced allocation
could not be utilized fully. The reason being given non-receipt of Utilization Certificates by
the implementing agencies. The Committee finds this disheartening. Interestingly, in BE
2015-16, the Plan allocation for this scheme which was `200 crore in BE 2014-15 has been
reduced to `95 crores. The Committee fails to understand with this meager allocation how
the objectives of the Department are going to achieved in time. We have more than 50%
reduced allocation for this Scheme and we are not able to spend even the highly reduced
allocation that too on technical procedural grounds as UCs. The Committee finds that if this
is the state of affairs in respect of this Scheme then future of this scheme remains highly
bleak. The Committee, therefore, recommends the Ministry to make all out efforts to
implement this scheme with the required zeal and dedication. (Para 43)
SPORTS UNIVERSITY IN NORTH-EAST
It has come to the notice of the Committee that till date no expenditure has been
incurred on account of National Sports University. The Committee recommends that setting
up of the proposed National Sports University is accomplished within the stipulated time and
the Department will go all out in this endeavour and make it a novel scheme. (Para 45)

20
NATIONAL SPORTS TALENT SERARCH SCHEME (NSTSS)
The Committee recommends that the requisite initiatives should be taken by the
Department to accomplish NSTSS within the stipulated time frame and all hurdles coming
in the way of the execution of the scheme are taken care of effectively so as to make it
a note-worthy scheme. (Para 47)
ENHANCEMENT IN SPORTS FACILITY OF JAMMU AND KASHMIR
The Committee appreciates the allocations of funds for expanding and development
of sports in Jammu and Kashmir which has been ridden with terror and insurgency for
quite a long time. The Committee hopes that improved sports culture in the region would
provide better channels to the youth to show their talent. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Department will work to get the proposed scheme implemented within
the required time and all impediments are overcome adequately, making this a worth-while
scheme. (Para 49)
PROMOTION OF SPOR TS AMONG DISABLED
The Committee gathered that a three days 15 th National Para-Athletics Meet was held
at Ghaziabad (U.P.) in March, 2015. The Committee is surprised that the complete apathy
and negligence was shown towards the para-athletes during this 15 th National Para-Athletics
Championship. The last Para-Olympic national Championship was held in 2013 at Bengaluru.
A win at this event of Ghaziabad would have ensured that athletes qualify to participate in
upcoming Para-games to be held in May in Delhi and then make a bid to Para-Olympic
Games in 2016. The Committee strongly recommends that a thorough inquiry may be made
to identify the persons responsible for this kind of fiasco and for taking appropriate action
against the persons concerned and to ensure that this does not recur in future. The
Committee desires to have a status note on it at the earliest. (Para 52)
The Committee has also gathered that the Paralympics Committee of India (PCI),
owing to lackadaisical attitude and apathy towards its athletes, has been suspended by the
International Paralympics Committee (IPC). The Committee also shows its concern for
chaotic condition prevailing in PCI for several years mostly due to individual conflicts and
proper management, etc. (Para 53)
PENSION TO MERITORIOUS SPORTS PERSONS
The Committee fails to get any reason for this reduction in RE from the
Department. The Committee doubts whether this scheme of the Department will achieve the
desired result in the current fiscal. The Committee, therefore, feels that a review may be
made of the scheme to include necessary ingredients in it to make it more comprehensive.
(Para 54)
HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT IN SPORTS
The Committee is surprised to find that `10 crore was allocated in BE 2014-15 and
it got reduced to `0.35 crore in RE stage of year 2014-15 owing to receipt of less number
of viable names. The Committee hopes that this scheme of the Department will achieve the
desired result in the current fiscal for what it has been meant for. (Para 55)

21
NATIONAL SPORTS DEVELOPMENT FUND (NSDF)
The Committee finds it disheartening that the budgetary allocation was reduced to

for the better utilization of funds. (Para 56)
NATIONAL DOPE TESTING LABORATORY
The Committee notes with satisfaction for the projected outcomes of achieving drug
free sports environment to the extent possible. (Para 57)
NATIONAL ANTI DOPING AGENCY (NADA)
The Committee appreciates that functioning of NADA and hopes that our
sportspersons get complete information on the guidance regarding banned drugs in sports
so that they are not misled in this regard. The Committee also hopes that this scheme of
the Department will achieve the desired result in the current fiscal only if it gets full
support as the by way of providing sufficient funds and required expertise. (Para 58)
WORLD DOPING AGENCY (WDA)
The Committee hopes that this scheme of the Department will achieve the desired
result in the current fiscal for what it has been meant for. (Para 59)
SAI STADIA RENOV ATION

Committee hopes that this scheme of the Department will achieve the desired result in the
current fiscal for what it has been meant for. (Para 60)
NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF SPORTS SCIENCE AND SPORTS MEDICINE
The Committee hopes that this scheme of the Department will become functional
during the current fiscal. (Para 61)
NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF COACHING EDUCATION
The Committee is surprised to see that such a significant scheme which is highly
needed in the country could not be finalized for the last two years. It is not clear why the
provisions are being made for this scheme in the Budget when scheme is under finalization;
why not make allocation in the year when the scheme has been finalized. Blocking funds

does not understand why this scheme could not be finalized. The Committee recommends

NATIONAL PHYSICAL FITNESS PROGRAMME-RESOURCE CENTRE AT LNIPE GWALIOR
The Committee hopes that this scheme of the Department will become functional
during the current fiscal. (Para 63)

22
SCHEME FOR IDENTIFICATION AND NURTURING OF SPORTS TALENT
The Committee hopes that this scheme of the Department will become functional
during the current fiscal. (Para 64)
NATIONAL WELFARE FUNDS FOR SPORTS PERSONS

Working Women’s Hostele
Recommendation (Para No. 11)

The Committee is of the view that the though there is acute shortage of working
women’s hostel in the country the Department could not achieve the physical targets. During
1993-94, but ambitious targets have been fixed for 1994-95. The Committee desires that
effective steps should be taken by the Department to achieve the targets set for 1994-95.

Ministry’s reply :

The reason for non-fulfilment of physical target in number of hostels in 1993-94 was the
steep rise in construction costs. However, capacity achievement over 82% and under-
utilisation was more than the BE/RE. To achieve the target of sanctioning of 60 additional
hostels to provide accommodation to 3000 working women during 1994-95 all the State
Governments and Union Territories have already been advised to send the proposals of all
suitable organisations. 50 proposals have already been received and are being processed.
Comments of the Committee

The Committee is not satisfied with the reply given by the Department and hence
reiterating its recommendation suggests that all-out efforts be made to achieve the physical
target.
Recommendation (Para No. 12) ~

In view of the frequent complaints received about mismanagement of the hostels
receiving grants and assistance from the Government, the Committee felt that there was
need for evolving some system of monitoring so as to control any sort of irregularities in
these hostels. For-this purpose, the Committee recommended that a Government representa-
tive be included on the Board of Management of each of such hostels.

“Since inception of the Scheme in 1972-73, 685 hostels for 44,960 working women have
already been sanctioned upto 31.3.1994. It will, thus, not be practicable to nominate a
Member of the Central Government on the Hostel Management Committee of each and
every Hostel. It has already been provided in the scheme that the Hostel Management

Comments of the Committee

The Committee expresses it isfaction over the present system of monitoring as it

alternative mechanism is required to be evolved by the Government to monitor the

functioning of various hostels.

Atrocities against Women
Recommendation (Para No. 16)

The Committee expresses its concern over the increasing number of cases of atrocities
against women and recommends that Government should conduct some review of these
publicity programmes to find out whether these are sufficient to create a significant impact
on the public mind.

Ministry’s reply

“Owing to the diverse nature of the programmes funded so far, this Deptt. has not so
far carried out any review of the nature suggested by the Committee. However, now since
most of the assistance under the programme is being given for legal literacy programmes,
this Deptt. would consider reviewing these legal literacy programmes in the future.”

Comments of the Committee .

Ever-increasing incidence of atrocities against women, specially in the urban areas, is
not only a matter of serious concern, but also a clear-cut reflection of the fact that the
programme has miserably failed to deliver the goods. Inspite of this, the Department does
not seem to have shown any concern as is obvious in its comments. The Committee is not
happy about this kind of apathetic attitude of the Deptt. and suggests that a periodic
evaluation of the efficacy of all the programmes in general, and this programme is particular,
must be undertaken to achieve the desired result.

The Committee expresses its deep concern over the fact that though the scheme was

“The Department has made concerted efforts to get the necessary approval for

Mahila Samridhi Yojana
Recommendation (Para No. 24)
The Committee is of the view that various programmes under the Mahila Samridhi

Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS)
Recommendation (Para Nos. 28 & 29)

The main thrust of ICDS programme is on the provision of Anganwadis in every village
and urban slum areas. Generally, there is one Anganwadi for a population of 1000 in rural
areas and urban slum areas and of about 700 in tribal areas, which is run by an Anganwadi
worker, a female voluntary worker and a helper. By the end of 1993, 3120 ICDS projects
were sanctioned which benefited about 1.94 crores children and women. For the year 1994-
95 an outlay of Rs. 426.00 crores has been approved for the ICDS and 200 new projects are
likely to start. The Committee feels that a big portion of the increased outlay is likely to be
absorbed in the increased honorarium to Anganwadi workers. Therefore, the Committee
feels that the amount available for the projected expansion of the scheme to cover new areas
is likely to be insufficient. Of 5239 blocks, 2119 blocks remain to be covered. At the rate, of
200 projects per year, it will take another 10 years for all blocks to be covered. To expedite
the process, any shortfall in the projected expansion by the end of the 8th Plan should be
properly estimated and additional allocations made.

The relative success of the ICDS scheme in improving child health and lowering IMR is
due to its decentralized and popular structure. Probably because of this, ICDS is being
increasingly seen as an umbrella organisation within which other schemes could be
incorporated. Thus early childhood education is now a part of ICDS. There is a new scheme
for adolescent girls; and creches and day care centres are sought to be made a part of ICDS.
Indira Mahila Yojana, in its revised form, will become a component of it. Separate
allocations have been proposed for these schemes by the Department. But the National
Creche Fund has only been notified. Allocation of Rs. 8 crores for Indira Mahila Yojana has
not yet been approved. Therefore, the Committee recommends that until and unless
separate additional allocations have been obtained for these additional components, ICDS
should concentrate on strengthening and expansion its own. structure with whatever
allocations it may get. The proposal to entrust a percentage of ICDS schemes to NGOs
should be properly assessed before it is implemented, since, in the absence of community-
based monitoring arrangements, it would be difficult to ensure accountability of NGOs.


Ministry’s reply

It is proposed to sanction 200 projects during the year 1994-95. In order to sanction 200
projects and to maintain the existing projects, the Plan outlay of Rs. 426 crores has been
approved for the ICDS which is adequate to meet the requirements. However, for
universalisation of ICDS during the 8th Plan period, we would require an additional amount
of Rs. 1166.27 crores in the Central plan and an additional amount of Rs. 1379.96 crores in
the State outlays on nutrition during the Plan period.

As mentioned against Para 28, the outlay provided for 1994-95 would be adequate to
meet the requirement of additional 200 blocks of ICDS project and to maintain the existing
ICDS projects. A number of effective steps including sanction of additional AWCs,
construction of godowns/anganwadi buildings, provision of storage containers have been
taken by the Department for strengthening ICDS scheme directly involvement of NGOs in
directly implementing ICDS projects has been considered vital to strengthening community
participation under the scheme. To ensure that only competent NGOs are entrusted with
such projects. State Governments have been given the discretion to identify competent
NGOs with proven track record.

Comments of the Committee

In view of the prospects of the universalisation of ICDS, the Committee feels that the
financial allocation earmarked for it is not adequate. Therefore, it suggests that allocations
for this scheme should be adequately enhanced. The Committee expresses its concern over
integration of more and more components under umbrella of ICDS without providing
adequate resources for each of them. The Committee, therefore, is of the view that due
consideration should be given to this aspect.

Recommendation (Para Nos. 33 & 34)

The Committee observes that out of the three components of ICDS, namely executive,
workers and recipients, two do not appear to be happy with the service. Therefore,
monitoring system should be strengthened to ensure proper functioning of the ICDS to the
satisfaction of all its components.

The Committee feels that since it is a Central project, public representatives should also
be involved for proper monitoring of the scheme.

Ministry’s reply

The Department has adopted an improve management information system to monitor
the implementation of the ICDS scheme. The Monthly Progress Reports on each aspect of
the Scheme is received by the Department straight from the projects which are analysed with
respect to crucial indicators on a quarterly and half yearly basis. Monitoring system has been
strengthened to reflect the frequency as the delivery of services and gender specific
information of the beneficiaries. In addition to these reports on performance of projects, the
Department is also receiving Quarterly Monitoring Reports on health aspects of the scheme
from the Central Technical Committee. These Quarterly Monitoring Reports are generated
by Central Technical Committee on the basis of Monthly Monitoring Reports received from
Primary Health Centres and analysis is carried out for variable such as provision of
supplementary nutrition, pre-school education, health check-up and referral services, child
and mother mortality, existing status of malnutrition of children, staff position, their recruitment
and vacancy position and immunisation coverage. The State exhibiting poor performance in
respect of any of these indicators are promptly addressed to rectify the suitably by intensifying
efforts and close monitoring. In addition to the existing monitoring system at the Central and
State level, the community based monitoring mechanism has been recently evolved. The States
have been asked to constitute Bal Vikas Mahila Samities at the village, block and district levels
for involvement of elected women representatives of Panchayats in monitoring all the child and
women programme being implemented in their area of jurisdiction.


Comments of the Committee

The Committee notes that the Department has not responded on the ICDS workers
being not happy with the services they are being over burdened with the integration/addition
of new schemes to the ICDS for which they are not being adequately compensated, suggests
that efforts should be made to remove the grievances of the ICDS workers.

Creches/Day Care Centres
Recommendation (Para No. 35)

This scheme was started in 1975 to provide day care services to children in the age
group of 0—5 years of those families whose monthly income does not exceed Rs. 1800 per
month. The scheme is implemented through the Central Social Welfare Board, the Indian
Council for Child Welfare and Bharatiya Adim Jati Sewak Sangh. During the year 1993-94,
a total amount of Rs. 23.05 crores was sanctioned to benefit about 3 lakh children. The
same amount has been allotted in the budgetary provisions for this year. The Committee
reaffirms its earlier observations made in its third report about the Bharatiya Adim Jati
Sewak Sangh regarding the need for conducting an enquiry into the affairs of the Sangh.

Ministry's reply
“During the current financial year a budget provision of Rs. 23.05 crores has been made

under the scheme of Creches and Day Care Centres. An evaluation of the creches
programme by competent professionals is underway.”

Comments of the Committee

The Committee is constrained to observe that the Department has taken the
recommendation in a very casual and cavalier manner by eschewing unequivocal reply on
conducting an enquiry into the affairs of the Bharatiya Adim Jati Sewak Sangh. Many more
cases of malpractices and irregularities in creche programmes being run by Indian Council
for Child Welfare, Central Social Welfare Board, apart from Bharatiya Adim Jati Sewak
Sangh, coming to the fore, has added to the urgency and necessity of such an enquiry.
Although the Committee has been subsequently informed that the inquiry has been initiated,
it underlines the need to expedite the process.

Recommendation (Para No. 39)

It has been observed that since Creche and Day Care Centres are non-expanding
schemes, the budgetary allocation remains stagnant. With escalation of costs, this may cause
maintenance grants to existing centres to dry up. Therefore, even non-plan allocation should
be enhanced. Also, until the National Creche Fund actually starts functioning, some scope
for expansion should be kept in the budgetary allocations under this head, in view of the
urgent need for such centres.

Ministry’s reply

The Department will sanction new creches under National Creche Fund. The National
Creche Fund has been set up. In accordance with Government policy, non-plan expenditure
is to be curtailed as far as possible. The Committee, however, would be happy to know that
the norms of nutrition as well as honorarium of the creche, scheme have been revised
upwards and adequate. provision for this expenditure has been made on the plan side with
the approval of the Planning Commission.


Comments of the Committee

The Committee is happy to note that the National Cultural Fund would start functioning
from this year, however, there may be many areas where NGOs may not be available for
running creches. In such areas where there are creches/day care centres under the old
system, these centres should not be allowed to suffer.

SAARC Decade of Girl Child

Recommendation (Para No. 41)

The Committee notes with concern that the SAARC Decade of the Girl Child, except
for one scheme introduced as a component of ICDS for the adolescent girl, has not found
any reflection in the budget. Schemes to improve the nutritional status of the girl-child and
schemes to prevent their dropping out from schools may be formulated. As for the National
Plan of Action for children, the Committee was informed by the Secretary that there was no
separate allocation for this in the Department’s budget because this plan is to be
implemented by different ministries and departments and Women and Child Development
Department is only the coordinator. Since, however, there is little evidence of such
coordinating activities so far, the Committee is constrained to conclude that this has not
made much headway so far and recommends its speeder planning and implementation.

Ministry’s reply

Government takes note of the concerns expressed by the Standing Committee at the
mere token provision for the National Plan of Action of Girl Child in the budgets of this
Department. We would like to clarify that the implementation of the Plan of Action and the
attainment of goals that have been quantified in the Plan of Action constitute the joint
responsibility of all Ministries/Departments of the Government and the modal Department
of Women and Child Development implementing programmes having a bearing on the girl
child. A token provision has been kept in mind the future need, if any, of introducing
special interventions for filling up critical gaps as and when felt necessary. This plan and the
National Plan of Action for Children would help the Department of Women and Child
Development to coordinate and orchestrate the working of various programmes run different
Ministries/Departments for the purpose of reaching the goals of children and girl children.

The Standing Committee has referred to the need for schemes to improve the
nutritional status of the girl child and-preventing school dropouts. It is submitted that girl
children upto the age of 6 years are already included within the ICDS programme which is
the world’s largest integrated child development programme and the specific problem of
school dropouts amongst girls is addressed through the Adolescent Girl Programme which
covers school dropout adolescent girls in the age group 11—18 years. This Department is
coordinating a special gender disaggregated monitoring of the ICDS Programme, the
programmes of the Department of Education, the programmes of the Department of Health
and Family Welfare and those of the other departments. Government, through the
Department of Education, extends special incentives to the girl children viz. free supply of
text-books, special hostel facilities, scholarships, uniforms, appointment of lady teachers etc.
for coordinating the entire effort, there is an inter-ministerial Coordination Committee under
the Secretary (WCD) at the Central level. We have also advised the State Government to
draw up similar action plans and set up similar State level Coordination Committees.

The Committee observes that the Department in its reply has not given any details of

Food & Nutrition Board
Recommendation (Para No. 43)

The Committee observes that the thrust of the policy should be on raising the
nutritional status of the population through ICDS, as well as nutritional education. In this
contest, the Committee recommends revival of the scheme of supply of milk to the under-
nourished school children.

Ministry's reply

The thrust of the policy of Food & Nutrition Board is already on raising nutritional
status of the population through nutritional education. For this purpose, demonstration
programmes are arranged by the field units of FNB and also training is given to housewives
and adolescent girls in nutrition education and preservation of fruits and vegetables.
Integrated Nutrition Education Camps and Orientation Training Courses are organised by
the field units of FNB for the supervisory and grassroot functionaries of different
Departments of State Government concerned with health and nutrition education. The
recommendation regarding supply of milk to school children has been sent to Department of
Educaiton for necessary action.

Comments of the Committee

The Committee finds that the Department in its reply has stated that the recommenda-
tion regarding supply of milk to school children has been sent to the Department of
Education for necessary action. The Committee feels that the Department should see to it
that the scheme of the supply of milk is revived and for this it should pursue the matter with
the Department of Education effectively.

Proliferation of Schemes

Recommendation (Para No. 44)

The Committee feels that, year after year, the focus of attention of the Deptt. keeps on
changing from one scheme to another and there seems to be no long-term perspective.
Therefore, the Committee recommends that instead of framing new schemes every year and
letting the earlier ones to just continue, the Deptt. should concentrate on some major
schemes and work to achieve the targets through suitable action plan.

Ministry’s reply

“Over the years, the Department has formulated policies and programmes dealing with
various aspects of the development of women and children according to changing needs,
imperatives and perspectives. The Department, thus, has a long-term perspective in both the
sectors. In the fields of child development, the Department plays a nodal role in
coordinating the development of children in various sectors, besides implementing its own
programme of Nutrition, Integrated Child Development and Early Childhood Education.
The Department’s continuing focus has been on working as the national machinery for
women, promoting the incorporation of women, as well as for moulding societal attitudes.
Besides this, the Department has a three-pronged approach to Women’s Development
through its own programmes targeted at training and economic empowerment, provision of


8

support services and awareness generation. Thus, the approach is a mix of advocacy and
action. However, as and when the need arises, new activities are taken up by the
Department. For example, the political empowerment of women as a result of 73rd
Constitution Amendment, has opened up possibilities of fundamental and significant
initiatives to be taken jn this field. Similarly, the adoption of National Nutrition Policy in
1993 has resul.ed in 8. greater focus on the issues of nutrition surveillance and preparation of
a Plan of Action cutting across different sections.”

Comments of the Committee

The Committee is of the view that the Department should devise long term plan
perspectives and concentrate on continuing with them considerably for a longer time so that
their benefits could percolate down to the targeted populace. Conceiving new and new
programmes, year after year, without giving them a practical shape is not a healthy
phenomenon and yields nothing. The reply of the Deptt. does not indicate any specific
action proposed to be taken on its recommendations. The Committee, therefore, reiterates
that the focus of the Department should be on strengthening the on-going schemes and it
should not keep on shifting its priorities.

Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS)

The main thrust of ICDS programme is on the
provision of Anganwadis in every village and
urban slum areas. Generally, there is one
Anganwadi for a population of 1000 in rural
areas and urban slum areas and of about 700 in
tribal areas, which is run by an Anganwadi
worker, a female voluntary worker and helper.
By the end of 1993, 3120 ICDS projects were
sanctioned which benefitted about 1.94 crore
children and women. For the year 1994-95 an
outlay of Rs. 426.00 crores has been approved
for the ICDS and 200 new projects are likely to
start. The Committee feels that a big portion of
the increased outlay is likely to be absorbed in
the increased honorarium to Anganwadi work-
ers. Therefore, the Committee feels that the
amount available for the projected expansion of
the scheme to cover new areas is likely to be
insufficient. Of 5239 blocks, 2119 blocks remain
to be covered. At the rate of 200 projects per
year, it will take another 10 years for all blocks
to be covered. To expedite the process, any
shortfall in the projected expansion by the end
of the 8th Plan should be properly estimated
and additional allocations made.

The relative success of the ICDS scheme in
improving child health and lowering IMR is
due to its decentralized and popular structure.
Probably because of this, ICDS is being in-
creasingly seen as an umbrella organisation
within which other schemes could be incorpo-
rated. Thus early childhood education is now a
part of ICDS. There is a new scheme for
adolescent girls; and creches and day care
centres are sought to be made a part of ICDS.
Indira Mahila Yojana, in its revised form, will
become a component of it. Separate allocations
have been proposed for these schemes by the
Department. But the National Creche Fund has
only been notified. Allocation Creche Fund has
only been notified. Allocation of Rs. 8 crores

approved. Therefore, the Committee recom-
mends that until and unless sperate additional

tional components, ICDS should concentrate

ture with whatever allocations it may get. The

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Human
Resource Development, having been authorized by the Committee, present this Two Hundred and
Seventieth Report of the Committee on the ‘Performance of National Sports Development Fund and
Recruitment and Promotion of Sportspersons’- Part I.
2. The Committee visited the Sports Complex and Regional Centres of Sports Authority of
India at Kolkata, Bengaluru and Mumbai. The Committee held wide ranging discussions with a
number of outstanding and distinguished sportspersons including Padamshri, Arjuna and
Dronacharya awardees, coaches, representatives of  National/State-Level Federations/Associations.
The Committee also heard the views of representatives of SAI, UCO Bank, United Bank of India,
Allahabad Bank, Coal India Limited Damodar Valley Corporation, Central Bank of India, State Bank
of India, Union Bank of India, Bank of India, IDBI Bank, Bank of Maharashtra, Bank of Baroda,
Dena Bank and LIC, Indian Oil, BPCL, HPCL, Air India, BEML, BEL, HAL, Canara Bank, State
Bank of Mysore, Vijaya Bank, Syndicate Bank and Corporation Bank to have an idea about their
contribution to the National Sports Development Fund and to explore how they can promote sports
and recruitment of sportspersons.
3. The Committee also interacted with the Secretary, Department of Sports, Additional
Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Secretary, Department of Financial Services (DFS),
Secretary, Department of Public Enterprises, Secretary, Department of Personnel and Training and
Director General, Sports Authority of India (SAI) in its meeting held on the 17
th July, 2015.
4. The Committee considered the Draft Report on the subject and adopted the same in its
meeting held on the 10th August, 2015.
5. The list of witnesses heard by the Committee on the subject is attached in Annexure.
6. For facility of the reference, observations and recommendations of Committee have been
printed in bold letters at end of Report.

REPORT
INTRODUCTION
Sports and games are an integral component in the all round development of human
personality. Apart from being a means of entertainment and physical fitness, sports also played
a great role in generating the spirit of healthy competition and bonding within the community.
Although India has a large population, its achievements in international sports have not been
commensurate. Considering the fact that Indian population is one of the youngest population
in the world, India has an immense potential in developing into a powerhouse of sports.
Through its various sports promotional schemes/programmes, the Government, nurtures talent
in youth, and provides them with requisite infrastructure, equipments, coaching facilities and
competition exposure for overall development of sports. It is a known fact that excellence in
sports has a great bearing on national prestige and morale of the country. Thus Government
spending on sports is an important indicator of the promotion of sports. There is no denying
the fact that India is lagging far behind the other countries in achieving excellence in the
sports. One of the reasons for this state of affairs is lack of funding in the sports sector. The
Government of India and the State Governments together spend only around 3 paise per capita
per day on sports which highlights the low level of spending on sports. Worldwide sports
sector has a mix of private and public investment. In India it is largely a State funded activity.
As the next Olympic games are approaching, the focus is once again on sports, skill
augumentation, training, coaching, competition, state of art equipments and better support
services to the sportspersons.
2. In the light of this background, the Committee decided to discuss broadly the subject
‘Promotion of Sports’ during its visit to Kolkata, Mumbai and Bengaluru from 1st to 7th July,
2015. While discussing the promotion of sports, sports promotion policies and fund mobilization
for sports with the public sector banks/public sector undertakings the Committee discovered that
most of the Public Sector Banks and Public Sector Undertakings did not have any definite and
uniform sports promotion policy in the first place. Further, they were also unaware of the existence
of the National Sports Development Fund created by the Government of India to promote sports
in a sustained manner. The question of contributing to that fund as a social responsibility was not
of much importance to them. In view of this scenario, the Committee also decided to deliberate
upon the performance of National Sports Development Fund and interact with all the stakeholders
on the issue.
(I)
PERFORMANCE OF NATIONAL SPORTS DEVELOPMENT FUND
3. The Central Government had established the National Sports Development Fund (NSDF) in
1998 under the Charitable Endowment Act, 1890, with a view to mobilizing resources from the
Government as well as non-governmental sources, including the private/corporate sector and non-
resident Indians, for promotion of sports and games in the country. In order to make contributions
to the fund attractive, cent percent exemption from income tax was made available on all the
contributions to the National Sports Development Fund. Financial Assistance is given from NSDF
to the Following:

2
— to outstanding sportspersons, sports federations and other organizations;
— top level sports persons who are medal winning prospects in Olympics,
Commonwealth Games, Asian Games and other international competitions;
— assistance is given for customized training to sportspersons both in India and abroad
to prepare them for winning medals at international events;
— special support to the sportspersons who have been selected under the programme
TOP (Target Olympic Podium), a Scheme, specifically devised to train medal prospects
for Olympic 2016 and 2020; and
— financial assistance is given to reputed organizations/institutes, engaged in the
promotion of sports and games for specific projects like creation of infrastructure,
procurement of state of art equipment etc.
4. It will not be out of place to mention here that in 1995 the Department-related Parliamentary
Standing Committee on Human Resource Development in its 34
th Report on “India’s Performance
in International Sports” had recommended as under:-
“The Committee feels that the Government alone cannot deliver the goods. Public and
Private Sectors’ involvement is necessary in supplementing the governmental efforts. The
Committee, therefore, emphasizes the need for a joint and coordinated approach by all the
agencies, including public and private sectors, in pooling their resources to promote sports
in the country. This is particularly necessary in the context of financial constraints, both
at the Central and State levels”.
5. At that time, the Committee discussed at length the involvement of Public and Private sector
in the Promotion of Sports. The Committee had detailed interactions with many reputed Public and
Private sector companies/undertakings such as TISCO, ITC, Hinduja, Escorts, UCO Bank, SBI,
IOB, BHEL, IOC, ONGC, Air India, Indian Airlines, SAIL, Peerless, Sanghi Group, CIL, Punjab and
Sind Bank etc. on the subject.
6. The Committee, in its above Report, had also recommended that each major industrial
house, both public and private sector, should be asked to adopt one sports discipline and they
should take the total responsibility of scouting talent and nurturing the same, including their
participation in various national and international events. On reciprocal basis, the concerned
industrial house should have its nominee in the concerned national federation/association. The
Committee again reiterates its recommendation and also suggests that major industrial
house should adopt, at least, one sport discipline and nurture the same if sports culture in
this country is to be evolved.
7. It also emerged out of those deliberations, that contributions were being received from
organizations at that time also but there was no mechanism for keeping and managing that
contribution. After the above said Report of the Committee, the Ministry of Youth Affairs and
Sports and Government of India (GOI) had established the National Sports Development Fund in
1998. However, since its inception adequate funds could not be collected which indicates that
the Department did not make sincere efforts to approach the Corporate and the Public
sector for contribution to the Fund.
8. In its 34th Report the Committee had also pointed out that there has been a lot of
duplication of efforts by the various sports control boards and bodies like Railways, P&T, Banks,
Steel Plants etc. in promotion of sports without any co-ordination with each other. The Committee
had further pointed out that there was also a lack of co-operation and communication between
different bodies, boards, SAI and sports federations. The Committee was not happy with the
chaotic situation and the lack of co-ordination between the various bodies leading to wastage of
scarce funds and time.

3
9. The Committee finds that the situation has not improved till now. The NSDF corpus
is still scarce, not many public and private organizations are coming forward to contribute
to the Fund and there is a lot of overlapping in promotion of sports as respective
organizations are following their own pattern so far as development of sports is concerned.
Further, the Committee notes that even from the scarce resources available with the NSDF,
there is laxity on the part of the Department in spending the same which shows lack of
commitment on the part of the Department to promote sports in true earnest. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department of Sports and SAI should take
steps to evolve an effective mechanism for regular dialogue and co-ordination with the
sports boards of the various organizations and federations so that duplication of efforts and
wastage of precious time and scarce fund is avoided.

11. The Committee learnt that BCCI gave maximum contribution to NSDF. However, the
income tax exemption was denied to them. The income tax authorities stated that BCCI was
engaged in cricket, so their involvement in other sports is not justified. The Committee considers
this the most bizarre justification to extract income tax. The Committee feels that Revenue
Department has not understood the spirit of NSDF. Many organization whether PSUs, Banks or
Private Organization have their own core business, however, they have been contribution to the
cause of sports, while the BCCI being richest sports body is morally bound to help other sports
in the country.
12. The Committee hopes that in future also, the BCCI will give its generous contribution. The
Committee also directs Department of Revenue to understand the spirit of NSDF as the
contributions towards this Fund cannot be charged for income tax. If at all this has been done in
the past it should be reversed with true sportsman spirit.
13. During its interaction with the Public Sector Banks and Public Sector Undertakings at
Kolkata, Mumbai and Bengaluru on the promotion of Sports and contribution to NSDF, the

under the aegis of Coal India Sports Promotion Association (CISPA) which is an
autonomous body, registered under West Bengal Societies Registration Act, 1961 in
2013.
— However, under the Sports Policy of Coal India Limited there is a provision that all
coal companies will contribute @25 paise per tonne of coal produced (in the previous
year) and non-coal producing companies will also contribute as per decision taken
from time to time to the corpus for CISPA for conducting promotional activities
regarding sports and culture.

7
— As far as ONGC is concerned the representative added that ONGC was allocating 2%
of Net Profit every year to CSR as per the guidelines of Government of India, and

14. From the above discussions the Committee can conclude that most of the Public
Sector Banks and Public Sector Undertakings were not aware of the existence of the
National Sports Development Fund or were linking it with the Corporate Social
Responsibility (CSR) activities.
15. The Committee also found that the Banks and CPSUs were spending crores of rupees
every year independently in the name of sports mainly for entertainment purposes or for
their commercial publicity in the form of giving sponsorship to tournaments, annual meets
smaller cash awards at local levels, except some of them like ONGC, Indian Oil, Air India,
HAL and a few banks. There is no coordination/linkage of any kind amongst them in this
regard. The Committee also found that the direction of and the manner which sports
activities are being done is not going to develop sports in the country. The Committee is
not for stopping such activities being undertaken by banks/PSUs, it feels that the monies
currently being spent could be put to much better use if a good part of it goes to NSDF,
a centralized and specialized mechanism for the development of sports in the country. It
also came up during the deliberations with these PSUs/Banks that they were ready to put
good amount of money to this Fund and some of them even promised to do so in future.
The Committee was in fact happily surprised to know this and felt encouraged to take up
this issue with the concerned Secretaries to the Ministries/Departments at Delhi to impress
upon them to find out if some kind of guidelines/norms, formal or informal could laid down
and an inter-ministerial body could be created for promoting, coordinating and monitoring
this Fund. The Committee feels a good amount of funds can be allocated that way to be
better used for the sports development.
16. Against this backdrop, the Committee decided to further deliberate on the issue.
Accordingly, the Committee heard the Secretary, Department of Sports along with Director General,
Sports Authority of India (SAI), Secretary, Department of Financial Services, Secretary Department
of Public Enterprises, Secretary, Department of Personnel and Training and the Additional
Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs on the issue of contributions to the National Sports
Development Fund in its meeting held on the 17th July, 2015.
17. The Secretary, Department of Sports informed the Committee that sports primarily is a
State subject. However, the Department of Sports along with the Sports Authority of India and
National Sports Federations played a very important role for sports and sportspersons at national
and international level. Training, coaching and participation at international level by sportspersons
were the main activities requiring greater financial resources. For this purpose beside the central
budgetary support, the Department had created the National Sports Development Fund to channelize
the corporate sector contribution for promotion of sports. He further submitted that, so far, only
limited resources had been tapped under the National Sports Development Fund and the Department
would strive to engaged Public Sector Banks/Public Sector Undertakings to contribute more to the
NSDF.
18. The Secretary, Department of Financial Services informed the Committee that there were
only 26 public sector banks, 4-5 Insurance Companies and 4-5 other financial institutions under the
Department. Since the Banks were not companies, the provisions of the Companies Act were not
applicable to them and there was no responsibility on the Public Sector Banks to spend minimum
two per cent on CSR activities. In spite of this, the banks had been doing good work under CSR

8
activities. He mentioned that some of the financial institutions, however, were adopting particular
sport and contributing to NSDF. He suggested that provision of the Companies Act regarding
spending of two per cent of the profit under CSR should be made applicable to the private
companies also. On the point of contribution by the Public Sector Banks to NSDF, he submitted
that Banks could only be requested to contribute.
19. The Secretary, Department of Public Enterprises stated that schedule VII of the Companies
Act mentioned only five funds, namely, Fund for Swachh Bharat Kosh, Fund for Clean Ganga,
Fund for Prime Minister’s National Relief and Fund for T echnological Incubation in Academic
Institutions. He suggested that the National Sports Development Fund could be made part of that
schedule so that Companies  could contribute to NSDF also. From the above discussion, the
Committee feels that there is an urgent need to focus on the following aspects of NSDF.
Publicity for National Sports Development Fund
20. From the Committee’s extensive deliberations with the stakeholders, it clearly
emerged that many public sector organizations and institutions were not aware of the
existence of the NSDF, its mandate and purpose. Most of the organizations mixed it with
the Corporate Social Responsibility. The Committee observes that the Department of Sports
should take steps to widely publicize the NSDF, its mandate, function and achievements to
attract contribution from all the Public and Private Sector Institutions. The Department
should publish a booklet on NSDF, highlighting its mandate, purpose, mode of contributions
to the fund by the stakeholders, and its achievements in promoting sports.
21. The Committee also recommends that once a sportsperson is selected for financial
support under NSDF or by the PSB/PSU/organizations, that financial support should continue
till the time the sportsperson attains a certain level. There should be no break in the
financial support to a sportsperson as the same could lead him/her to-drop out of the sports.
Thus, financial support should be on continuous basis.
Inclusion of NSDF in Schedule VII of the Companies Act
22. The Committee notes that another suggestion put forth by the stakeholders was that
NSDF should be included in Schedule VII of the Companies Act. The Committee
recommends that the Companies Act should be amended accordingly, once it is included in
Schedule VII, not only the government sector companies/PSUs but also private companies
will start making contributions to this Fund. This will certainly ensure continuous and
consistent fund flow to NSDF.
23. The Committee further feels that the Public Sector Banks while contributing their
funds for the promotion of sports may bifurcate their contribution in two segments. They
can contribute to the National Sports Development Fund and at the same time can approach
schools/colleges in rural areas and, if possible, adopt one of the sports by investing in
infrastructure and other sports facility in the schools/colleges in the rural areas.
24. The Committee, therefore, recommends that this contribution to NSDF for promotion
of any recognized sports, sports academy/a group of elite athletes may be allowed and
specifically mentioned as permissible activity for CSR contribution to ‘Funds’ specified in
Schedule VII of the Companies Act, 2013. In view of poor upkeep maintenance of our SAI
Centres and need for modern equipments/facilities in them, the contribution to SAI for
construction repair, modernization of sports infrastructure/operation such as talent search
and development; national/regional competitions maintenance with respect to its regional
centres, STCs, SAG Centres, NSAs may be specifically mentioned in permissible CSR

9
expenditure under CSR Rules by issuing a circular from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
The Department of Sports may follow this up with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
Further, the Committee feels that mandatory CSR provision need to be made applicable
with respect to Insurance and Banking Sector as well as Companies Act does not cover
them.
25. The Committee also recommends that a certain percentage of Education Cess may be
earmarked for sports promotion as it is our integral part of education as per the Education
Policy. This could be around 0.25 percent for sports leaving 2.75 percent for education. The
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports may follow it up with the Ministry of HRD and
Ministry of Finance for this purpose.
Wider Representation in Council And Executive Committee of the National Sports
Development Fund
26. For the management and administration of NSDF, a council is constituted by the
Central Government. This council has representation from the Ministry of Youth Affairs and
Sports, SAI and eminent sportspersons representing corporate sector, private foundations
and non-profit voluntary organizations. The Committee feels that if the Department of
Sports expects adequate funding from the Public Sector Banks and Public Sector
Undertakings, it should give adequate representation to the other concerned Ministries and
organizations on the council. The Committee, accordingly, recommends that 4-5 PSUs/
Banks/Private bodies/Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Department of Financial Services and
Department of Public Enterprises should be given representation in the council. Similarly,
day to day working of the Fund is managed by an Executive Committee which have
representation from the Ministries of Youth Affairs and Sports and Human Resource
Development only. The Committee feels that the Executive Committee should also have
wide representations for managing the day to day working of the Fund. Accordingly 4-5
PSUs/Banks/Private bodies/Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Department of Financial Services
and Department of Public Enterprises should be given representation in the Executive
Committee also.
27. The Committee also takes this opportunity to point out that the scheme of NSDF was
framed in the year 1998. At that time, Youth Affairs and Sports was one of the Department
under the Ministry of Human Resource Development. This explains the presence of the
representatives of the Ministry of Human Resource Development in the composition of the
council and the Executive Committee. Now that the Department of Youth Affairs and Sports
has become a full fledged Ministry, the presence of the representatives of the Ministry of
Human Resource Development seems to be inconsistent in the scheme. The Committee,
accordingly, recommends the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to relook into the
provision and amend it accordingly.
II
RECRUITMENT AND PROMOTION OF SPORTSPERSONS
28. The Recruitment and Promotion of Sportspersons is also one of the important areas meriting
serious consideration. Accordingly, the Committee took up this issue also during its study visit to
Kolkata, Mumbai and Bengaluru while interacting with PSBs and PSUs.
29. The representative of CIL submitted that direct recruitment of Sportsperson having National
and/or International repute was being done. Such recruitment was done on the recommendations

10
of Apex Body after observing different procedural formalities as per norms of the Company at

58. The Secretary, Department of Sports submitted that the DoPT, Government of India had

Further, there is no mechanism to monitor  the implementation of the guidelines which is why
there is no unpublished data to maintain about this either in CPSUs or in Government
Ministries/Departments. As result, we do not know whether sportspersons are being recruited

Secretary, Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) submitted that the Department was the

recruitment and service matters. He informed that as far as recruitment was concerned there
was a policy since 1984 for recruiting sportspersons but the Department of Public Enterprises
had done an exercise in 1997 where guidelines were made. Central Public Sector Enterprises
(CPSE) had reached a certain level of maturity and decided to withdraw 696 guidelines one of

59. The Committee feels that both recruitments and promotions of sportspersons were
not being given due importance. Current guidelines prescribe that Boards of Banks/PSUs
and other organizations set aside up to 5 per cent of posts to be filled by sportspersons. In
the absence of mandatory minimum cap, the banks/PSUs and other organizations have been
recruiting sportspersons in varying percentage. This is creating confusion. The Committee,
accordingly, recommends that DoPT should make at compulsory for all the Ministries/
Departments to recruit 5 per cent sportspersons. The Committee would further appreciate
if DoPT gives clear instructions to all the Ministries/Departments/organizations to
effectively implement its promotion policy for the sportspersons. The Committee further
observes as follows:-
(i) Job reservation for Sportspersons may be made mandatory in Central
Government, its subordinate officers and undertaking including banks and
insurance companies;
(ii) 2 per cent vertical and 3 per cent horizontal reservation may be made
mandatory in case of shortfall in vertical reservation due to 50 per cent limit
getting breached, it should automatically get transfer to horizontal reservation;
(iii) In pay band II and III reservation for sportsperson may also be allowed for
Olympic medalist and equivalent; and
(iv) SAI can function as nodal agency and work as employment exchange for
recruitment of sportspersons.
60. It has been learnt from the representation of Anju Bobby George that DoPT circular
dated 26th July, 2012 was being restricted to the appointees from 2012 onwards when the
guidelines were re-issued and provision of three out of turn of promotions was made. The
Committee recommends that this circular should be construed as a guideline by all the
departments and they should have liberal interpretation and should not restrict it and
implement it from prospective date. This is clarificatory guideline and must be applicable in
case of all existing players. Hence, the Committee directs the Department of Customs and
other Departments that if the existing players have not been given out of turn promotions
in their career, they must be considered for three out of turn promotions in phased manner
making the post personal in case the player/employee has won medals in the /international
sporting events during the course of employment even before 2011. Such players should not
be counted as normal department employees and parity should not be drawn with regular
employees. These players are ambassadors and pride of concerned organization who are
considered as role model. The Committee also appreciated Department of Customs for
recruiting and retaining such world class players. The Department should handle such

18
players with care, dignity and respect and encourage them to provide guidance, coaching and
lecture to youngsters in schools and colleges and in the sporting complexes. They should

Department may also come forward in establishing academies or adopting some coaching

— “Sports persons/coaches of various Government departments and public sector

— Many sports persons in various departments are struggling with sports training and

national coaching camps/competitions (Domestic and international) up to the year 1999

system available/in place, and all the national coaches are treated uniformly, irrespective

— The foreign coaches and technical staff are offered contract amount differently and
usually it varied from 5000 US$ to 1500US$ per month. The Committee finds that

achievements for our country. The Indian coaches with better profile, records and
commitment and integrity are side lined due to vested interests or lack of interest.
Indian coaches who have made most outstanding results at World level should be
treated at par with foreign coaches in remuneration and other support.
— Indian coaches like Pullela Gopi Chand, Robert Bobby George, U. Vimal Kumar, etc

— This approach would definitely destroy the top most coaches of India. The Foreign

— That sports quota appointments has reduced substantially in the recent years in many

centre and found that sub-standard material was used in the laying of the running track. The
Committee also found that the football ground did not have proper turf for playing. The Committee
was anguished to  see that many of the shooting ranges were not properly maintained.
66. The Committee recommends that SAI and the Department of Sports should give
funds for proper maintenance of the sports facilities at SAI centres in India. The
Department of Sports should also ask the PSUs, PSBs and other organizations to adopt one
of the sports disciplines and improve the facilities at the SAI centre.

separately for each award. The promotion should be without reference to the vacancies, test,

Sports and games events while representing the country would be eligible for one additional
increment. Each of the Medals received would be considered as a separate medal for the purpose
of extending this benefit under the scheme in the International Sports or Games meet. Further, an
employee was eligible for maximum of five increments under this scheme during his/her entire
service.

68. The Committee in its 34th Report on the India’s Performance in International Sports in 1995
had made the following observations on the restructuring of Sports Authority of India (SAI):-

administrators, particularly most of the officials of the Sports Authority of India (SAI)
had no sorts background. It was cited as one of the reasons for lack of direction in the
sports arena.’

functioning of the Sports Authority of India (SAI). It was complained that SAI had
become a huge and unwieldy organization, with completely bureaucratic characteristics.

not originally contemplated. There are a number of square pegs in the round holes. It

are strengthened, we cannot expect better results from them. Work and accounts of the

having any sports background. The Committee feels, the situatiop requires immediate
corrective steps.

72. The Committee was informed that there is lack of good coaches for giving training
to juniors in the SAI centres. The Committee feels that there have been many outstanding

feels that such sportspersons with their experience and expertise could nurture and bring
up a new generation of sportspersons besides providing much needed financial help to
retired sportsperson.
73. While deliberating on the subject it was brought to the notice of the Committee that
BCCI was giving pension to its retired cricketers. The Committee feels that SAI should also
devise a mechanism to provide pension to the sports persons from NSDF after they retire
from active sports life. This would serve as a social security for the sports person and they
would be able to level their life independently and with dignity.

22
Sportspersons not to be Engaged in Day to Day Administrative Work
74. The Secretary DoPT had stated that many departments are engaging sportspersons in day
to day administrative work and some time they are engaged in the official work from 10-12 hours
daily. Such sportspersons are treated as regular employees and Departments assign them routine
work. The Secretary had pointed out that it was against the norms for which the sportspersons
has been recruited. He stated that it was understandable that there is shortage of manpower in
every department and regular recruitments have also not been done by certain departments, but
engaging sportspersons for such routine work is not the solution.
75. The Committee took serious note of the fact that organisations/departments, which
are recruiting sportsperson, engage them in day to day administrative work of the
organisation. The Committee feels that recruitment of a sportsperson in an organisation is
a value addition to that organisation and instead of engaging him/her in Administrative
Work, he/she should be given opportunity to excel in the sports and also to train and
mentor junior sports persons.

76. The Committee was also given to understand that the foreign coaches engaged by
various bodies/organisations were being paid higher remuneration vis-a-vis the Indian
coaches. The Committee feels that this practice is uncalled for if we desire to promote
sports in the country. The Committee would appreciate if grading of coaches is done and
equal and uniform remuneration is paid to both foreign and Indian coaches.
