RECOMMENDATION/OBSERV ATIONS AT A GLANCE
(I)
PERFORMANCE OF NATIONAL SPORTS DEVELOPMENT FUND
The Committee had also recommended that each major industrial house, both public
and private sector, should be asked to adopt one sports discipline and they should take the
total responsibility of scouting talent and nurturing the same, including their participation
in various national and international events. On reciprocal basis, the concerned industrial
house should have its nominee in the concerned national federation/association. The
Committee again reiterates its recommendation and also suggests that major industrial
house should adopt, at least, one sport discipline and nurture the same if sports culture in
this country is to be evolved. (Para 6)
The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports and Government of India (GOI) had
established the National Sports Development Fund in 1998. However, since its inception
adequate funds could not be collected which indicates that the Department did not make
sincere efforts to approach the Corporate and the Public sector for contribution to the
Fund. (Para 7)
The Committee finds that the situation has not improved till now. The NSDF corpus
is still scarce, not many public and private organizations are coming forward to contribute
to the Fund and there is a lot of overlapping in promotion of sports as respective
organizations are following their own pattern so far as development of sports is concerned.
Further, the Committee notes that even from the scarce resources available with the NSDF,
there is laxity on the part of the Department in spending the same which shows lack of
commitment on the part of the Department to promote sports in true earnest. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department of Sports and SAI should take
steps to evolve an effective mechanism for regular dialogue and co-ordination with the
sports boards of the various organizations and federations so that duplication of efforts and
wastage of precious time and scarce fund is avoided. (Para 9)
From the above discussions the Committee can conclude that most of the Public
Sector Banks and Public Sector Undertakings were not aware of the existence of the
National Sports Development Fund or were linking it with the Corporate Social
Responsibility (CSR) activities. (Para 14)
The Committee also found that the Banks and CPSUs were spending crores of rupees
every year independently in the name of sports mainly for entertainment purposes or for
their commercial publicity in the form of giving sponsorship to tournaments, annual meets
smaller cash awards at local levels, except some of them like ONGC, Indian Oil, Air India,
HAL and a few banks. There is no coordination/linkage of any kind amongst them in this
regard. The Committee also found that the direction of and the manner which sports
activities are being done is not going to develop sports in the country. The Committee is
not for stopping such activities being undertaken by banks/PSUs, it feels that the monies
currently being spent could be put to much better use if a good part of it goes to NSDF,
a centralized and specialized mechanism for the development of sports in the country. It
also came up during the deliberations with these PSUs/Banks that they were ready to put
23

24
good amount of money to this Fund and some of them even promised to do so in future.
The Committee was in fact happily surprised to know this and felt encouraged to take up
this issue with the concerned Secretaries to the Ministries/Departments at Delhi to impress
upon them to find out if some kind of guidelines/norms, formal or informal could laid down
and an inter-ministerial body could be created for promoting, coordinating and monitoring
this Fund. The Committee feels a good amount of funds can be allocated that way to be
better used for the sports development. (para 15)
Publicity for National Sports Development Fund
From the Committee’s extensive deliberations with the stakeholders, it clearly
emerged that many public sector organizations and institutions were not aware of the
existence of the NSDF, its mandate and purpose. Most of the organizations mixed it with
the Corporate Social Responsibility. The Committee observes that the Department of
Sports should take steps to widely publicize the NSDF, its mandate, function and
achievements to attract contribution from all the Public and Private Sector Institutions.
The Department should publish a booklet on NSDF, highlighting its mandate, purpose,
mode of contributions to the fund by the stakeholders, and its achievements in promoting
sports. (para 20)
The Committee also recommends that once a sportsperson is selected for financial
support under NSDF or by the PSB/PSU/organizations, that financial support should continue
till the time the sportsperson attains a certain level. There should be no break in the
financial support to a sportsperson as the same could lead him/her to drop out of the sports.
Thus, financial support should be on continuous “basis. (para 21)
Inclusion of NSDF in Schedule VII of the Companies Act
The Committee notes that another suggestion put forth by the stakeholders was that
NSDF should be included in schedule VII of the Companies Act. The Committee
recommends that the Companies Act should be amended accordingly, once it is included in
schedule VII, not only the government sector companies/PSUs but also private companies
will start making contributions to this Fund. This will certainly ensure continuous and
consistent fund flow to NSDF. (Para 22)
The Committee further feels that the Public Sector Banks while contributing
their funds for the promotion of sports may bifurcate their contribution in two
segments. They can contribute to the National Sports Development Fund and at the
same time can approach schools/colleges in rural areas and, if possible, adopt one of
the sports by investing in infrastructure and other sports facility in the schools/
colleges in the rural areas. (Para 23)
The Committee, therefore, recommends that this contribution to NSDF for
promotion of any recognized sports, sports academy/a group of elite athletes may be
allowed and specifically mentioned as permissible activity for CSR contribution to ‘Funds’
specified in Schedule VII of the Companies Act, 2013. In view of poor upkeep
maintenance of our SAI Centres and need for modern equipments/facilities in them, the
contribution to SAI for construction repair, modernization of sports infrastructure/
operation such as talent search and development; national/regional competitions
maintenance with respect to its regional centres, $TCs, SAG Centres, NSAs may be
specifically mentioned in permissible CSR expenditure under CSR Rules by issuing a

25
circular from the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. The Department of Sports may follow this
up with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. Further, the Committee feels that mandatory
CSR provision need to be made applicable with respect to Insurance and Banking Sector as
well as Companies Act does not cover them. (Para 24)
The Committee also recommends that a certain percentage of Education Cess may be
earmarked for sports promotion as it is our integral part of education as per the Education
Policy. This could be around 0.25 percent for sports leaving 2.75 percent for education. The
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports may follow it up with the Ministry of HRD and
Ministry of Finance for this purpose. (para 25)
Wider Representation in Council and Executive Committee of the National Sports
Development Fund
For the management and administration of NSDF, a council is constituted by the
Central Government. This council has representation from the Ministry of Youth Affairs
and Sports, SAI and eminent sportspersons representing corporate sector, private
foundations and non-profit voluntary organizations. The Committee feels that if the
Department of Sports expects adequate funding from the Public Sector Banks and Public
Sector Undertakings, it should give adequate representation to the other concerned
Ministries and organizations on the council. The Committee, accordingly, recommends that
4-5 PSUs/Banks/Private bodies/Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Department of Financial
Services and Department of Public Enterprises should be given representation in the
council. Similarly, day to day working of the Fund is managed by an Executive Committee
which have representation from the Ministries of Youth Affairs and Sports and Human
Resource Development only. The Committee feels that the Executive Committee should
also have wide representations for managing the day to day working of the Fund.
Accordingly 4-5 PSUs/Banks/Private bodies/Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Department of
Financial Services and Department of Public Enterprises should be given representation in
the Executive Committee also. (Para 26)
The Committee also takes this opportunity to point out that the scheme of NSDF was
framed in the year 1998. At that time, Youth Affairs and Sports was one of the Department
under the Ministry of Human Resource Development. This explains the presence of the
representatives of the Ministry of Human Resource Development in the composition of the
council and the Executive Committee. Now that the Department of Youth Affairs and Sports
has become a full fledged Ministry, the presence of the representatives of the Ministry of
Human Resource Development seems to be inconsistent in the scheme. The Committee,
accordingly, recommends the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to relook into the
provision and amend it accordingly. (Para 27)
II
RECRUITMENT AND PROMOTION OF SPORTSPERSONS
DoPT Circulars on Recruitment and Promotion of Sportspersons
The Committee feels that both recruitments and promotions of sportspersons were
not being given due importance. Current guidelines prescribe that Boards of Banks/PSUs
and other organizations set aside upto 5 percent of posts to be filled by sportspersons. In

26
the absence of mandatory minimum cap, the banks/PSUs and other organizations have been
recruiting sportspersons in varying percentage. This is creating confusion. The Committee,
accordingly, recommends that DoPT should make at compulsory for all the Ministries/
Departments to recruit 5 percent sportspersons. The Committee would further appreciate if
DoPT gives clear instructions to all the Ministries/Departments/organizations to effectively
implement its promotion policy for the sports persons. The Committee further observes as
follows:-
(i) Job reservation for Sportspersons may be made mandatory in Central
Government, its subordinate officers and undertaking including banks and
insurance companies;
(ii) 2 percent vertical and 3 percent horizontal reservation may be made mandatory
in case of shortfall in vertical reservation due to 50 percent limit getting
breached, it should automatically get transfer to horizontal reservation;
(iii) In pay band II and III reservation for sports person may also be allowed for
Olympic medalist and equivalent; and
(iv) SAI can function as nodal agency and work as employment exchange for
recruitment of sportspersons.   (Para 59)
It has been learnt from the representation of Anju Bobby George that DoPT circular
dated 26 th July, 2012 was being restricted to the appoints from 2012 onwards when the
guidelines were re-issued and provision of three out of turn of promotions was made. The
Committee recommends that this circular should be construed as a guideline by all the
departments and they should have liberal interpretation and should not restrict it and
implement it from prospective date. This is clarificatory guideline and must be applicable in
case of all existing players. Hence, the Committee directs the Department of Customs and
other Departments that if the existing players have not been given out of turn promotions
in their career, they must be considered for three out of turn promotions in phased manner
making the post personal in case the player/employee has won medals in the /international
sporting events during the course of employment even before 2011. Such players should not
be counted as normal department employees and parity should not be drawn with regular
employees. These players are ambassadors and pride of concerned organization who are
considered as role model. The Committee also appreciated Department of Customs for
recruiting and retaining such world class players. The Department should handle such
players with care, dignity and respect and encourage them to provide guidance, coaching and
lecture to youngsters in schools and colleges and in the sporting complexes. They should
also be encouraged to establish own academies/coaching centres or associate themselves with
SAI or Ministry of Sports for sporting activities like coordination and motivation etc. The
Department may also come forward in establishing academies or adopting some coaching
centres where their talent could be utilized. (Para 60)
The Committee noted that most of the sports persons were being recruited in pay
bands I and II jobs only. The Committee feels that this practice should be rectified. A
player gives, the most productive years of his life to sports. Therefore while recruiting
these sportspersons they should be treated at par with pay band III officers based on their
sports ac hievements at National and International level. The Committee would appreciate if
this aspect is also considered by the DoPT in right earnest. (Para 62)

2. At the outset, the Chairman welcomed the Members to the meeting of the Committee
convened to hear the Secretaries, Department of Financial Services, Department of Public
Enterprises, Department of Personnel and Training and Department of Sports along with
Director General, Sports Authority of India and Additional Secretary, Ministry of Corporate of
Affairs, on the Promotion of Sports and Recruitment of Sportspersons in Central Public Sector
Undertakings and Public Sector Banks.
3. The Secretary, Department of Sports, submitted before the Committee that additional
resources are required for creating more job opportunities for sportspersons. Sports being a
State subject, the grass-root developmental works are only done by the State Government.
Nevertheless, Sports Authority of India, Department of Sports along with National Sports
Federations play important roles in national team selection, customized coaching, international
events participation, etc. He explained that the National Sports Development Fund was
created from contributions from different corporate sectors which are given 100 per cent tax
exemption. The major contributors to this fund are BCCI, Jaiprakash Industries and India
Infrastructure Finance Corporation Limited. To solicit contributions from corporate sector,
the Department of Sports has developed different structures, some of which are direct
contribution to the National Sports Development Fund, adoption of a particular game,
adoption of a particular athlete, etc. Target Olympic Podium is a new scheme introduced by
Department of Sports where top athletes, who are likely medal prospects in the forthcoming
2016 and 2020 Olympic Games, are identified and supported. The funds for this Scheme are
totally borne out of National Sports Development Fund. Regarding the issue of providing
more career opportunities to the athletes, the Department of Personnel and Training has
formulated a policy where upto 5 per cent of the positions can be taken out of the purview
of normal selection boards and be filled up by sportspersons. The major recruiters of
sportspersons are Railways, Defence Services, ONGC and Oil Companies. However, many
other Public Sector Undertakings have a long way to go in recruiting sportspersons.
Therefore, there is a need for formulating a policy for employment of sportspersons in
Public Sector Undertakings and Public Sector Enterprises. He submitted that there is also a
need to work out a policy as to how the sporting talent of sportspersons can be further
utilised in sports once their active playing career is over, as most of the sportspersons, after
recruitment, are totally disconnected or disassociated with the game that they have played all
their lives and because of which they have been recruited.
4. The Additional Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, submitted that the activities
included in Corporate Social Responsibility are decided by the Company’s Board and the
Government of India does not have any say beyond a certain limit. A high level committee has
been constituted to monitor the contributions made by various private organizations and Public
Sector Undertakings under Corporate Social Responsibility and the report of this committee is
expected at the end of August, 2015. He informed that under the new Companies Act, the
companies with `1000 crores of turn over or above or `500 crores of net worth or above or
`5 crores of profits or above have to spend 2 per cent of their average net profit in the
preceding three financial years on CSR activities. He pointed out that National Sports
Development Fund has not been included in Schedule VII of the Companies Act but sports, in
general, have been mentioned.
5. The Secretary, Department of Financial Services, pointed out that as banks are not
registered under the Companies Act, it is not mandatory for them to contribute under Corporate
Social Responsibility. He pointed out that, so far, 1903 state level and national level players
have been recruited in various Public Sector Enterprises, not only in clerical cadres, but also

34
in officer cadres. The Bank which recruited the highest number of sportspersons is State Bank
of India, having recruited 420 sportspersons, the other banks are Vijaya Bank, Syndicate Bank,
Central Bank of India, Bank of India etc.

recruiting sportspersons since 1984. However, the Department of Public enterprises, in 1997,
suspended many guidelines and among them were the guidelines for recruitment of
sportspersons. He apprised the Committee that, in consultation with the Department of
Personnel and Training, he would examine if there is a need for the said guideline to be
circulated again. He explained that Corporate Social Responsibility is under Schedule VII of the
Rules as notified by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs which contains five funds, of which four
of them are Fund for Swachh Bharat Kosh; Fund for Clean Ganga; Fund for Prime Minister’s
National Relief and Fund for Technological Incubation in Academic Institutions. However,
National Sports Development Fund is not included in that Schedule. He submitted that he would
take up the matter for inclusion of National Sports Development Fund in the Schedule VII with
the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
7. The Secretary, Department of Personnel and Training, submitted that since 1984,
they have issued a guideline whereby upto 5 per cent seats of group ‘c’ and ‘D’ jobs may
be reserved for sportspersons. However, this guideline was withdrawn. He apprised the
Committee that efforts will be made to re-issue this guideline in all Public Sector
Undertakings. He also pointed out that another guideline was framed wherein
sportspersons, who won medals in Olympic Games, Commonwealth Games, Asian Games
and World Championships, would be given out of turn promotion. He iterated that these
guidelines must be applied in the most transparent manner so that deserving candidates get
these opportunities. A policy was also framed that sportspersons, who are recruited in
various Public Sector Undertakings, must be allowed to play until their sporting careers are
over.

REPORT  
 
 
INTRODUCTION 
 
1. The Country has such a big untapped sports poten tial, however compared to it, the 
performance of sports is abysmal.  Modern competiti ons are about the physical conditioning and 
not merely about the physic ability and Indians nee d to understand it soon to be able to compete at 
the International level.  Possessing a good built a lways gives an edge but at the end of the day it is  
about the skills you possess and the zeal to succee d in the sport.  Conceptualize at the Chinese, 
Japanese or Koreans, they don’t necessarily possess  an intimidating body structure like that of the 
Europeans and African.  But they have dished out st erling performances across various sports and 
have acquired positions in the Olympic tables.  So lack of physic ability is not the bane for the 
Indian players. Physical conditioning have become v ery important in contact sports today and it 
has become imperative for sportspersons to be assisted by the specialists. 
 
2. Our players are very hard working and eager to l earn.  Their dedication is just impeccable 
and all they need is the correct guidance and mento rs, of course, under whom they can sharpen 
their skills on the right path and direction.  The exposure and much needed experience can 
definitely turn the tables for the sports aspirants .  The management, players, training, etc., i.e. 
every aspect, of the preparation needs to be in top  notch.  We need to improve the area of our 
attitude towards the sport.  The high time is for c oncentrating on three very essential aspects, viz.,  
fitness levels, lifestyle and mental conditioning.  In past the Department of Sports/SAI have failed 
deplorably in all these three areas which culminated in wiping out medal winning hope for India in 
championships like Olympics, etc., compared to othe r Countries of world like U.S., Germany, 
England, China, Japan, Korea, etc. 
 
3. With modern sports being highly competitive, the  use of modern infrastructure, equipment 
and advanced scientific support has changed the sce nario of sports at the international level. 
Keeping in line with the growing demands for advanc ed infrastructure, equipment and scientific 
support, the Government has taken several initiativ es and is providing the necessary assistance to 
sportspersons by way of training and exposure in in ternational competitions backed up with 
scientific and equipment support. 

 
4. It is well known that sports is, primarily, a St ate subject in Country.  The Department of 
Sports along with the Sports Authority of India and , of course, National Sports Federations, 
however, have been playing vital role for promotion  of excellence in sports as well as broad- 
basing of sports.  The availability of adequate spo rts facilities including appreciable sports 
infrastructure throughout the Country is a basic ne cessity for broad-basing of sports.  In the 
direction of funding in sports sector, the Central Government had established the National Sports 
Development Fund (NSDF) in 1998 under the Charitabl e Endowment Act, 1890.  The Committee 
views the performance of NSDF as an important aspec t in mobilizing resources for development 
of sports and in this perspective, interacted with PSEs/PSBs as well as other stakeholders in the 
field of sports, which are described in the succeeding paras 
 
(I)  VISIT TO HYDERABAD

45. ‘ Pay and Play’ and ‘Come and Play' Schemes. 
These Schemes have been started by the SAI at its v arious Centres, in order to ensure the 
optimum utilization of the available sports infrast ructure and to earn some revenue. Individual 
sportspersons and organization could use this infra structure, for training on their own and 
competition purposes, on nominal payment. There is no provision for coaching, under this 
Scheme. This Scheme was launched at all SAI Centres , in the Country, on 1 October, 2011. The 
Scheme aims at mass participation in sports; system atic coaching support; talent spotting; and

The main objectives  of the fund are as under: 
/head2right To administer and apply the moneys of the Fund for promotion of sports in general and 
specific sports disciplines and individual sportspe rsons in particular for achieving 
excellence at the National and International level; 

/head2right To impart special training and coaching in relevant  sports disciplines to sportspersons, 
coaches and sports specialists; 
/head2right To construct and maintain infrastructure for promotion of sports and games; 
/head2right To supply sports equipments to organizations and in dividuals for promotion of sports and 
games; 
/head2right To identify problems and take up research and devel opment studies for providing support 
to excellence in sports; and 
/head2right To promote international cooperation, in particular , exchanges which may promote the 
development of sports 
/head2right To provide low interest or interest free loans for projects and activities related to any of the 
aforesaid objects. 
 
Council and Executive Committee of NSDF 
104. The Fund is managed by a Council constituted b y the Central Government.  Union Minister 
in charge of Youth Affairs and Sports is the Chairp erson of the Council and the Members of the 
Council include Senior Officers of the Department, representatives of apex industry bodies, Sports 
Promotion Boards of some organizations etc.   The C ouncil decides all policy matters relating to 
the Fund and frame rules and regulations for the ma nagement of the Fund.  The Council was last 
reconstituted in March 2012.  The last meeting of the Council was held on 04.06.2015. 
 
105. The day to day working of the Fund is managed by an Executive Committee.  Secretary 
(Sports) is the President of the Executive Committe e.  49 meetings of the Executive Committee 
have been held so far. The Executive Committee was last constituted in May 2014. 
106. Guidelines have been formulated, with the appr oval of the Council-NSDF, in order to 
streamline the procedure in NSDF Secretariat.  Thes e are intended for general guidance in 
processing proposals under NSDF without compromisin g the in-built element of flexibility 
available in the Scheme.  Any relaxation, in conformity with the special status/nature of NSDF and 
in public interest, is to be made with the approval of the Chairperson of the Council. 
 
107. The NSDF has given financial assistance to top  level sportspersons, who are medal 
winning prospects in Olympics, Commonwealth Games, Asian Games and other international 
competitions, for their customized training, both i n India and abroad; NSDF has also given 

assistance to Sports Federations for the preparatio n of teams for international competitions and 
other organizations. The other major area of assist ance is for creation of sports infrastructure.The 
NSDF has continued the assistance to potential sportspersons, who are medal prospects, with stress 
on the athletes selected under Target Olympic Podium (TOP) Scheme.  
 
108. The selected athletes have to sign an ‘Athlete  Grant Agreement’ which covers aspects like 
the privileges and obligations on the part of the a thlete and the Department of Sports/NSDF, code 
of conduct etc. The selected athletes are expected to give due recognition to the support given by 
the Department/NSDF; they may have to appear in spe cified promotional events being organized 
by the Department and the partners of the Scheme. T hough the TOP Scheme takes care of the 
normal requirement for customized training, the ath letes are free to take assistance from other 
sources for any additional items/facilities provide d these are not available under other general 
schemes of the Department. 
109. Based on the recommendations of the Identifica tion Committee, 97 Athletes and 09 Para 
Athletes (Total 106) have been selected so far. The  selection was made after a process of research 
and consultation with the concerned stakeholders by  the Committee. Total budget earmarked for 
the said 106 athletes is about Rs 50.00 Crore till Olympics 2016. The budget amount depends on 
each discipline of sports and the status (elite or emerging) of the athletes.121 sportspersons in 
various sports disciplines have been sponsored so f ar by the NSDF for their customized training 
(individual/group) under coaches of international repute as given below:

given to National Sports Federations in various dis ciplines (like Tennis, Judo, Rowing, Boxing, 
Wrestling and Athletics) for organizing group train ing/camps as part of preparation of players for

 Outcomes and Progress:  
111. The selected athletes will be provided financi al assistance for their customized training at 
Institutes having world class facilities and other necessary support.  Benchmark for selection of 
athletes under the scheme will be in relation to in ternational standards.  There will be annual/semi-
annual review of performance of selected athletes. 
112. A Committee namely, ‘TOP Scheme Elite Athletes  Identification Committee’ has been

for selection of the right candidates, review of pe rformance and operation of the scheme.  Shri 
Rahul Dravid, Shri Pullela Gopichand, Shri Abhinav Bindra and Ms MC Mary Kom are among

113.  The officials submitted that 36 athletes have  so far agreed to join the Scheme. 20 have 
submitted their programmes. Some of these programme s have been approved and assistance has 
started flowing to the athletes. India Infrastructu re Finance Company Limited (IIFCL), a PSU 
under the Ministry of Finance, has agreed to contri bute Rs. 30 crore to National Sports 
Development Fund (NSDF) by contribution of Rs. 10 c rore per annum for next three years.  
Contribution of Rs. 10 crore for 2015-16 has alread y been received.  Customized training at 
Institutes having world class facilities and other necessary support is being provided to the elite 
athletes, which would result in improved performanc e and a higher position in medals tally for the 
Country in international sports events and mega-sports events.

114. As on 20th March, 2015, 45 athletes have been identified from 6 disciplines namely 
athletics, badminton, boxing, shooting, wrestling a nd sailing have been identified as potential 
medal winners for Olympics 2016. Around 30 more ath letes are to be identified from archery and 
athletics. Out of the said 45 athletes, consent via email has been sent by 37 athletes, 23 have signed 
the agreement and 18 have given their programs / re quests for preparation for Olympics 2016. The 
programs received from athletes are vetted by the c oncerned National Sports Federation, coaches 
and experts. Based on the said feedback around Rs. 1 crore has already been released for 6 athletes 
namely Vikas Gowda (athletics), Abhinav Bindra, Hee na Sidhu, Manavjit Singh Sandhu, 
(shooting) , Aishwarya and Varsha (sailing). Furthe r around Rs. 88 lakhs is in the pipeline to be 
released shortly subject to submission of clarifica tions / documents by athletes from archery, 
shooting, wrestling and athletics. 
 
115.  All athletes are being contacted proactively by the Department to submit their programs for 
grant of financial assistance. Total estimated budg et for supporting 75 athletes from TOP scheme 
is around Rs. 40 to 45 crores till Olympics 2016. T he said support is over and above the support 
being provided by the Department under Scheme of assistance to NSFs through SAI.  
 
116. The Committee on the basis of deliberations wi th PSUs/PSBs for promotion of Sports 
reiterates its views that Public and Private Sector  Undertakings as well as Banks / Financial 
Institutions etc., may be encouraged by the Departm ent of Sports/SAI to adopt one Sports 

Discipline or can take total responsibility of scouting talents and its nurturing including their 
participation in various National and International  Events. On the reciprocal basis, the 
concerned donor should have its Nominee in the conc erned National Federal/Association. 
The Committee is seized of the fact that, GAIL has orally committed that they would adopt 
one Centre of SAI.  The ONGC has proposed to suppor t Wrestling players.  Further M/s 
Damodar Valley Corporation has also offered to supp ort two athletes under Target Olympic 
Podium (TOP) Scheme for which requisite information  as requested by them has been 
furnished to them.  The Committee directs that the Department of Sports and SAI should 
nominate an exclusive Nodal Officer in each region for co-ordinating with PSUs/PSBs so that 
they can contribute to the NSDF as well as adopt a Sports Discipline/Game or a Centre. The 
Committee directs the Department of Sports/SAI to submit  a monthly progress report to the 
Committee to this effect. 
 
117. The Committee is seized of the fact that many of the outstanding sportspersons of 
yesteryears are living in penurious circumstances.  The Committee desires that the 
Department of Sports should prepare a database of s uch players so that initiative may be 
taken by the Department of Sports to alleviate the financial condition of such sportsperson of 
yesteryears who have won medal or participated in N ational/International 
events/Championships by providing lump sum financia l assistance/lifelong pension facility, 
etc.  The Committee expects to send a progress report in this regard within a month. 
 
118. The Committee on the basis of its deliberation s with sportsperson and various stake 
holders in the field of sports decided to assess th e rate of employability of sportspersons in 
the country.  The Committee, therefore, desires tha t the Department of Sports should 
prepare basic database on the current status of emp loyment in Central Government/State 
Government departments, their PSUs, and PSBs  of sp ortspersons representing and winning 
medals in national/international events/championshi ps.  A status note is required to be sent 
to the Committee within a month. 
 
 
 
 
 

CONCLUSION 
 
 
119. The countdown for Rio Olympics 2016 is not far  away and this biggest sporting event will 
be watched around the world.  Indian Sports will ge t a chance to script history by their medal 
winning performance, after the toil of sportsperson  for the best part of four years and more.  In 92 
years of journey between 1924 and 2016, India has t he honour of one solitary individual gold 
medal in its kitty .  In a Country of such a humongous sports potentia l, the Committee hopes 
that this record can only get better.  The Committe e notes that we have to realize that where 
we stand for Rio 2016.  The performance of Indian c ontingent in the previous participation 
in Olympics is mostly about failure.  It is merely a question of when and where our 
sportsperson failed and blame game, as usual, where  accusations are exchanged among the 
involved people who refuse to accept any responsibi lity.  The defeat and losses bring 
disappointment.  The first and foremost question to  be asked is whether team or 
sportsperson fell short of expectations on account of poor training, exposure and  lack of 
amenities.  The Department of Sports/SAI, National Sports Federations etc., are in the 
process of zeroing in on the sportspersons possessi ng the medal winning prospects.  Keeping 
in view the breakdown of Indian contingent in past Olympics, the Committee expects the 
sportspersons to stand up to the pressure of Olympi cs and not to give a below par 
performance.

INTRODUCTION 
 
(I)  VISIT TO HYDERABAD 
 
 The Department-related Parliamentary Standing Comm ittee on Human Resource 
Development undertook a study visit to Hyderabad fr om 27 
th  to 29 th  October, 2015 to assess 
the performance of National Sports Development Fund  (NSDF), promotion of sports and 
recruitment of sportspersons in Public Sector Banks and Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs). 
            (Para 5) 
 
 From the deliberations of the Committee with CPSUs , it has come to notice that 
CPSUs are not adequately familiar with the existenc e of the National Sports Development 
Fund (NSDF) and they are by and large linking  the NSDF with CSR activities.  The 
Committee, therefore, directs the Department of Spo rts as well as the Sports Authority of 
India to take all possible measures immediately to educate all the CPSUs on the difference 
between NSDF and their role in CSR so that funds ca n be mobilized for NSDF without any 
further delay.  The Committee notes that the way th e CPSUs are participating on 
development and promotion of sports can be made mor e rationalized and contributing to the 
broad-basing of National Sports.  The Committee als o notes with anguish that this issue was 
also pointed out in its pervious Report on the same  subject, however, no action seems to have 
been taken in this regard and in case the awareness  and familiarity about the NSDF among 
the CPSUs continue to languish as on date, the very  purpose of the NSDF would be defeated 
and the Department of Sports /Sports Authority of I ndia would be responsible for the failure 
on their parts to popularize the same.      (Para 1 8)  
 
 The Committee, after its deliberations with PSBs, feels that though there are Sports 
Control Boards in these Banks, yet they are not awa re of the requirement for contribution to 
the National Sports Development Fund for promotion of excellence in sports, as well as 
board-basing of sports. The Committee notes that th e Department of Sports and the Sports 
Authority of India have not properly familiarized N SDF to them and the role required from 

them in this regard.   The Committee appreciates th e periodic encouragement given by 
Banks to sports as well as sportspersons in the for m of holding tournaments/sports events,   
cash awards, contribution as sponsorships, etc.  Ho wever, co-ordination with Department of 
Sports/SAI is lacking.  The Committee recommends th at Department of Sports/SAI should 
make concerted efforts in co-ordinating with them i n promotion of sports in the perspective 
of extant National Sports Policy and encouraging th em to make contribution to the National 
Sports Development Fund.        (Para 25)

of sports from the Central Government through the D epartment of Sports and the need and 
identification of projects are made under different  extant schemes.  The Committee 
recommends that it would be an appreciative move if  the Department of Sports and the SAI 
interact with the State Governments for encouraging  the recruitment of sportspersons in 
vacancies arising out in the domain of State Governments of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana 
covering their autonomous units as well.  The Commi ttee directs to provide a status note in 
this regard from the Department of Sports within a month.    (Para 28)

management and recommends that the respective autho rities of SAI are required to take

Recommendations/observations  
15 . On a specific query regarding vacancies in NYKS, the Committee came to know that as per 
DOPT instructions, cadre restructuring needs to be undertaken every 5 years.  However, the same 
has not been done in case of NYKS.  The Committee f eels that the current structure is flawed, 
resulting in serious stagnation in promotions which  poses some operational difficulties.  The 
Committee, accordingly, recommends that it is imper ative to take urgent initiatives to fill-up 
vacant posts in NYKS, especially in the category of  District Youth Coordinators (DYCs) (342 
vacancies) and Accounts-cum-Typists (ACTs) (210 vac ancies).  These vacancies are adversely 
affecting NYKS work.   The Committee was informed t hat the cadre restructuring proposal is 
being finalized in the Department to improve the op erational efficiency as well as promotional 
avenues without increasing the total strength.  The  proposal has been referred to Ministry of 
Finance for consideration and approval.  The Commit tee feels that efforts be made for filling up 
the vacant posts, by engaging a Government/PSU recr uiting agency and also by either taking 
persons on deputation or on outsourcing basis.  Ste ps be taken for filling up vacancies in other 
posts as well on urgent basis.  Besides, the Cadre restructuring be completed at the earliest as it 
aims at rationalizing existing staff strength with no additional financial burdening and it would 
ease out the problem to a great extent. 
 
Action Taken  
   
Regarding cadre restructuring of NYKS, the Ministry  of Finance, Department of Expenditure, has 
advised, vide their ID No.2(16)/E.III Desk/2015 dat ed 22.06.2015, that the Ministry may carry out 
the restructuring with the approval of the Governin g Body of the NYKS and the Minister-in-
charge, subject to the condition that (i) the proposal remains within the stipulated parameters of the 
cadre review and (ii) NYKS has finances to absorb t he extra expenditure/ the proposal is 
financially neutral. Accordingly, further necessary  steps are being taken to complete the process. 
Regarding filling up of vacant posts of District Yo uth Coordinators (DYCs) and Accounts Clerk-
cum-Typists (ACTs), NYKS has finalised the Recruitm ent Agency. Further steps are being taken 
to complete the recruitment process. Initially, 150  vacant posts of DYCs and 177 vacant posts of 
Accounts Clerk-cum-Typists are sought to be filled up.  Pending completion of regular recruitment 
process, steps are being taken to take officers on deputation/ outsourcing basis, so that work does

been selected this year. Second advertisement has b een issued for inducting more officers on 
deputation.

Recommendations/observations  
53. As regards augmentation of funds concerning differe nt schemes of the Department, the 
Secretary pleaded before the Committee that he woul d be striving for augmentation of fund 
allocations during the RE stage.  However, it is no t clear to the Committee as to how allocation of 
funds, in the perspective of the 14 th  Finance Commission, would be adjusted between the Centre 
and the States for the on-going schemes/programmes wherever the expenditure has to be borne by 
both.  The Committee shows its concern for the Depa rtment to clarify its stand on this count.  The 
Committee desires to have a note on this issue to be sent to it at the earliest. 
 
Action Taken  
 
 The Department has only one Scheme, namely, Nation al Service Scheme (NSS), where 
expenditure is shared between the Centre and the States, in the following ratio: 
 
a. In case of J&K and UTs (without legislature), the C entral Government provides 100% 
funding. 
b. In case of NE States (including Sikkim), Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, the sharing of 
expenditure between Centre and States is in the ratio of 75:25. 
c. In case of all other States/ UTs, the sharing of ex penditure between Centre and States is in 
the ratio of 7:5. 
 
As far as NSS is concerned, the Ministry of Finance , Department of Expenditure has already 
clarified, vide their OM No. 66(1)/PF.II/2015 dated  23.04.2015 that there is no change in the 

funding pattern (i.e. ratio of sharing of expenditu re between the Centre and the States) for NSS 
during 2015-16 and that it will remain the same as was during last financial year.  Thus, 
Department of Youth Affairs is so far not impacted by the ongoing exercise for restructuring of 
various centrally sponsored schemes.

NATIONAL SERVICE SCHEME (NSS)  
Recommendations/observations  
21. The Committee feels that the effective execution of  this scheme, in fact, leaves a lot to be

better to associate people, who are absolutely apol itical, i.e, scientists, engineers, social thinkers , 
etc., to have interactions with the students for gu iding and motivating them.  Their services may 
also be used to draw programmes for the benefits of  our young volunteers in the present situation. 
Availability of thirty-three lakhs volunteers is a big army.  They can do miracle if their energies 
are channelized positively.  People having knowledg e for the maintenance of communal harmony 
may also be associated to be effectively utilized f or achieving national integration, communal 
harmony, etc. 
 
Action Taken  
 
 In fact, the NSS follows a very dynamic framework,  which provides opportunities to take 
up any innovative activity with the broad area of ‘ voluntary community service’. In practice, a lot 
of innovations are taking place in every State/ UT.  These innovative activities are duly 
documented and brought out in the form of an Annual  Report by NSS Organisation. An important 
component of all NSS activities, esp. NSS Camps, is  “Suvichar”, under which eminent persons 
from different fields are invited to address NSS vo lunteers and to interact with them. NSS 
volunteers are put through 20 hours of orientation programme, during which eminent persons are 
invited to address the volunteers and to interact w ith them. Communal Harmony and National 
Integration are key themes of all NSS activities. A ctivities like NSS Mega Camps, Youth 
Festivals, North-East NSS Youth Festivals etc. help  in fostering the spirit of communal harmony 
and national integration. NSS volunteers play an ac tive role in all important initiatives of the 
Government. For instance, 8.92 lakh NSS volunteers participated in Yoga Programmes organised 
in various parts of the country on the occasion of International Day of Yoga (21 st  June, 2015). In 
addition, in the Programme at Rajpath, 700 NSS volunteers worked as Stewards (observers). Some 
significant achievements under NSS during 2014-15 were as follows: 
 
• 71.33 lakh saplings were planted by NSS volunteers. 
• 4.27 lakhs units of blood was donated by NSS volunteers. 
• 20.47 lakh children administered Pulse Polio drops by NSS volunteers. 
• 17,063 health/ eye/ immunisation camps were organis ed, in which 9.50 lakh volunteers 
 participated.  
• 30,538 awareness programmes/ rallies/ campaigns wer e organised on issues of relevance 
 to the community, in which 19.89 lakh volunteers p articipated.  
• 107.67 lakh volunteer-hours of Shramadaan was under taken by NSS volunteers during 
 the year. 
• 5 North East NSS Youth Festivals were organised, involving 1,500 youth. 

• 2 NSS Mega Camps organised in (i) Ladnun in Rajasth an and (ii) Majuli in Jorhat 
 District of Assam, with participation of about 880  NSS volunteers and programme 
 officers. 
• 1,453 NSS volunteers have participated in adventure activities. 
• Self-Defence Training was imparted to 1.88 lakh NSS volunteers. 
• 160 NSS volunteers participated in Republic Day Parade, 2015. 
 
NATIONAL YOUTH CORPS (NYC)  
Recommendations/observations  
23. The Committee finds out that under the NYC Scheme, NYKS is expected to be engaged 
more in convergence activities as well as different  projects/Special Programmes of different 
Ministries/Departments of Government of India being  undertaken by NYKS.  NYC volunteers are 
the backbone of NYKS.  They are the actual field fu nctionaries who assist in the implementation 
of programme and activities of NYKS.  It is through them that the youth even in the remotest areas 
may get awareness/benefit of the on-going schemes o f the Government.  But two volunteers per 
block, Committee feels is not sufficient which need s to be increased.  Besides, keeping in view the 
special circumstances in the North-Eastern States a nd 83 Districts affected by Naxalite violence, 
these areas need to have much more, may be 10 NYCs per block.  In addition more volunteers will 
be required for the 123 districts where NYCs is exp ected to come up with new Kendras in the 
coming months. The Committee was informed that as s uch total requirement of NYCs works out 
to 43,000.  The Committee expresses its concern abo ut just two volunteers in each block who are 
paid a meager honorarium of Rs. 2500 per month.  Th is amount has stagnated since the 
introduction of the scheme in 2010.  Recently, an E valuation Study of the Scheme was conducted 
through an independent agency, which recommended in creasing the Honorarium to improve the 
motivation level of the volunteers.  The Committee, accordingly, recommends that this honorarium 
should be made double, i.e at least @ Rs.5000/- per  month.  Furthermore, for accommodating this 
enhancement of honorarium, the Department is requir ed to make initiative for requisite increase in 
budget allocation.  
 
Action Taken  
 
 The matter was considered in the 46 th  Meeting of the Board of Governors of the Nehru 
Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS) held on 16 th  June, 2015, in which it was recommended that the 
number of NYCs may be increased from 2 to 4 per Blo ck and their honorarium may be increased 
from Rs.2,500/- to Rs.5,000/- per month. This will have the implication of increasing the funds 
requirement under NYC Scheme four-fold. Since NYC i s a Scheme of the Department, this 
requires approval of the Standing Finance Committee  (SFC).  Steps are being taken to complete 
the procedural requirements and obtain the necessary approvals.

YOUTH DEVELOPMENT INDEX (YDI)  
Recommendations/observations  
4. It has been learnt that the youth development index  (YDI) to serve as a ready reckoner for 
educators and policymakers has been proposed.  Ther e would be focus on developing qualities of 
good citizenship and community service amongst the youth besides inculcating in them the spirit 
of volunteerism.  They would be provided training a nd research support and encouraged to take up 
sports and adventure activities.  Youth travel woul d be promoted and initiatives would be taken to 
create an international perspective amongst them.  All this would be done by building on synergies 
with the activities of other Ministries, Department s and agencies.  Special focus would be on the 

rural youth.  These efforts would aim at channelizi ng youth energy in productive activities and 
engaging them in nation-building activities.  Align ed with this thinking, a National Youth Policy 
(NYP) - 2014 has been formulated through a consulta tive process. The Committee emphasizes the 
urgent need to develop YDI for making youth related  policies/ programmes that would be focused 
and effective.  It, therefore, should be done as soon as possible. 
 
Action taken  
  
In fact,  Rajiv Gandhi National Institute of Youth Developmen t (RGNIYD) under the Department, 
had developed India Youth Development Index (YDI), 2010 with technical support from Tata 
Institute of Social Sciences (TISS).  The Report wa s duly published. RGNIYD has now taken up 
the task of developing a revised and updated Youth Development Index. The Institute has 
constituted a Steering Group, comprising of eminent  persons from different backgrounds, for 
providing guidance in this regard. 
 
Comments of the Committee 
 
 The Committee finds that the Action Taken Notes, s ubmitted by the Department  is 
silent on the pivotal aspect of targeted time  for achieving this work of revision and updation 
of Youth Development Index.  The Committee notes th at the entrusted organization, i.e., 
RGNIYD for carrying out this task is itself  reelin g under the fund constraint and there is 
requirement of strengthening the faculty position o f the Institutes, which needs filling up of 
the academic posts urgently. The Department has giv en assurance to the Committee, 
germane to its recommendation vide para 34 that add itional allocations of fund would be 
sought at RE stage concerning RGNIYD for this purpo se. The Committee,  accordingly 
directs the Department to provide the details of ad ditional allocations it had sought at RE 
stage and also comment whether it would be adequate enough to meet the requirement. 
 
 
BUDGETARY ALLOCATION  
Recommendations/observations  
10. The Committee notes that the Department was given m uch lower amount this year than 
what it had projected; it got same amount in 2015-1 6 as given in previous fiscal.  Therefore, it 
leaves no scope for any expansion except continuing  with existing schemes, which is not a happy 
situation.  In view of reaping the benefits of demo graphic dividend, we have to empower the 
Department to undertake activities to empower our y outh in a big way.  The current level of 
allocations, in fact, does not reflect that approac h. Many of the major schemes launched by the 
Prime Minister, it appears are not factored into th e funds allocated. The Committee, therefore, 
recommends strongly to increase Department's alloca tion suitably at RE stage.  While 
recommending to increase the plan allocation for 20 15-16, the Committee likes to underline the 
good performance of the Department in terms of util ization of funds as well as achieving it targets. 
 It means, had the allocations been higher in line with its demands, the achievements also would 
have been still better. As a result, Department cou ld not propose/ undertake any revision/ 
expansion of its on-going activities. 
 
Action Taken  
 

 During 2015-16, all the schemes/ programmes are bei ng implemented with great sense of 
urgency. About 46% of the Plan Allocation has alrea dy been utilised by 31.08.2015. The pace of 
funds utilisation is expected to pick up further in  coming months. On the strength of this 
performance, proactive efforts shall be made for se eking substantial increase in allocations for the 
year at RE stage.   
 
Comments of the Committee  
 
 The Committee notes that inadequate allocation of f unds has remained the main 
constraint in effective implementation of schemes o f the Ministry. The Committee is helpless 
to make an assessment of the enhanced allocation of  funds at the RE stage as the acceptance 
of the revised budget proposals are still awaited f rom the Ministry of Finance.  Considering 
the performance of the Department in terms of utili zation of funds as well as achieving its 
targets, the Committee, therefore, can only await f or the intimation from the Ministry of 
Youth Affairs and Sports,  Department of Youth Affa irs with respect to enhancement of 
allocation of funds so that the demographic dividend of India should be put to greater use.  
 
NATIONAL SERVICE SCHEME (NSS)  
 
Recommendations/observations  
20. The Committee notes that NSS is a noble programme o f personality and character 
development of students through community service.  However, it currently covers less than 10% 
student’s strength eligible to join NSS.  This is m ainly due to inadequate funds allocations which 
have remained stagnant for last many years. Visuali sing the slightly enhanced allocation 
amounting to Rs.82.18 crores in RE 2014-15 in relat ion to Rs. 75.50 crores in BE 2014-15 for 
NSS, the Committee gathered that the increase in RE  was to clear the backlog expenditure. 
 Further, in regard to three components of activiti es under NSS, viz. volunteers performing 120 
hours of work; number of villages adopted; and adve nture activities, the Committee has been 
informed that there is no substantial shortfall in targets achievement by the Department with only 
exception of Adventure activities, that have to be suspended in 2015-16 on account of reduced 
allocation of funds, i.e., Rs. 70.15 crores in BE 2 015-16.  The Committee, therefore, recommends 
that there is a need to increase fund allocations.  The Department has informed that the States have 
been demanding upward revision of norms concerning financial assistance under NSS.  It seems 
justified to look into this aspect so that the prov ision of financial assistance gets increased.  The 
Committee specifically points out that NSS involves  organizing regular community service 
activities for at least 120 hours per volunteer per  annum and a special camp of 7-day duration in 
adopted village/slum. The Department should endeavo ur to fulfill the suggestions for providing 
them a Tee –Shirt and Cap with NSS Logo, NSS Badge and NSS Identity Card.  
 
Action Taken  
 
 The progress of utilisation of funds under NSS is very encouraging. About 73% of the 
allocation for 2015-16 was utilised by 31.08.2015. In view of pressing need for additional funds, 
an additional allocation of Rs.12 crores (under Pla n) has been made for NSS during the first 
supplementary stage this year, through internal app ropriation within existing overall budget 
allocation of the Department. As a result of this a dditional allocation, the adventure activities have  
now been taken up during current year.  Proactive e fforts will be made at RE stage for further 

increase in the allocation for NSS, so that the Programme implementation can be further improved. 
However, upward revision of norms for financial ass istance to States will be feasible only if the 
there is substantial step-up in the allocations. Th e current allocations are inadequate to even meet 
the funds requirement as per existing norms. As per  current norms, allocation is @Rs.475 per 
volunteer per annum. Instructions have been issued for providing NSS Badge and NSS Identity 
Cards, but provision of Tee Shirt and Cap would be possible only if the allocations are increased 
substantially. 
 
Comments of the Committee  
 The Committee notes that the adventure activities have been taken up in the current 
year.  However, the Committee expresses its concern  that the current allocations are 
inadequate to even meet the funds requirement as per existing norms.  The NSS is a centrally 
sponsored scheme with the objective to develop char acter and personality of youth.  
Therefore, the Department need not give up the init iatives on its part to get the funds raised 
for fulfilling the morale boosting efforts like, providing the Tee shirt and Caps with NSS logo 
to NSS volunteers. Due to the pending acceptance of  the budget proposals from the Ministry 
of Finance, the Department could not give any infor mation as to whether there has been an 
increase in the budget allocation for this scheme at RE stage.  
National Programme for Youth and Adolescent Development (NPYAD) 
28. The Committee, in the light of the resource sca rcity for this scheme, recommends that there 
is need for substantial increase in the fund alloca tion. The Department should follow-up for the 
increase in the fund allocation for NPYAD at RE stage. 
 
Action Taken 
 The allocation for NPYAD was reduced from Rs.32 cr ore in RE 2014-15 to Rs. 17.10 crore 
in BE 2015-16.  During the first supplementary stag e this year, an additional allocation of Rs.11 
crore (under Plan) has been made for NPYAD, through  internal appropriation within existing 
overall budget allocation of the Department. Proact ive efforts will be made at RE stage for further 
increase in the allocation for NPYAD, so that the P rogramme can be implemented smoothly and 
the intended objectives of this Programme can be achieved. 
 
Comments of the Committee 
 The Committee is of the view that it would be appr eciated if concerted efforts bring 
the result concerning fund allocation for NPYAD. On  account of scarcity of requisite funds, 
the intended role of an umbrella programme for assi stance to various organizations 
concerning youth and development activities cannot be played by NPYAD.  Whether there 
has been an increase in the fund allocation at RE s tage cannot be ascertained as the Ministry 
of Finance is yet to give its acceptance to the budget proposal sent by the Department. 
 
RAJIV GANDHI NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF YOUTH DEVELOPMENT (RGNIYD)  
 
Recommendations/observations  
33. The Committee is constrained to note that the Budge t provision for BE 2015-16 has been 
kept at Rs. 20.00 crore (inclusive of Rs.2 crore fo r NE), as there is no increase in the overall 
Budget allocation for the Department in 2015-16, wh ich is kept at the same level as during 2014-
15, i.e., Rs. 384.00 crore.  The Committee is surpr ised that the decrease in budget allocation for 

this scheme in RE 2014-15 amounting to Rs.15.86  cr ore  with respect to Rs.20.00 crore in BE 
2014-15 is on account of Non-submission of Utilization Certificate, it is unacceptable.  
 
Action Taken  
 
 During current year, the timely release and utilis ation of funds is being closely monitored, 
so that allocated funds are fully utilised and fund s do not lapse on account of non-submission of 
UCs etc.  
 
Comments of the Committee  
 
 RGNIYD is a nodal agency for training youth as a f acilitator of youth development 
activities in rural, urban and also tribal areas. However, to note that the budget provision for 
this ‘Institute of National Importance’ has been re duced to Rs. 15.86 crores in RE 2014-15 
due to lesser requirement of funds owing to non-sub mission of Utilisation Certificates is a 
very unfortunate situation. The Committee finds the  response of the Department very 
routine. The Committee would like to reiterate that  concerted and serious efforts need to be 
taken up for the proper and full utilisation of fun ds and also ensure timely submission of 
Utilisation Certificates.  
  
 
Recommendations/observations  
34. However, owing to the mandated assignments to RGNIY D and in view of the task of up-
scaling of multifarious activities of the Institute  to establish a brand image, the Committee firmly

has to play its intended role satisfactorily.  The Department is, therefore, required to continue 
follow-up for increasing allocations for RGNIYD. Th e Committee strongly recommends for 
initiating requisite initiatives so as to curb the delay in getting U.Cs which hampers further 
budgetary allocations.  As regards the need for str engthening the faculty position of the Institute, 
the Committee is not fully convinced with the expla nation of the department.  In order to 
strengthen the faculty of the Institute, the Commit tee feels the academic posts have to be filled 
with a sense of urgency.

 Proactive efforts will be made to utilise allocate d funds expeditiously and seek additional 
allocations at RE stage. Efforts are being made to expedite completion of the recruitment process 
for the existing vacant posts. The matter will be f ollowed up vigorously for sanction of additional 
posts as per the requirement of the Institute.

 Merely agreeing in principle by the Department to take up proactive efforts to utilise 
funds expeditiously and to expedite completion of t he recruitment process for the vacant 
posts, the Committee feels, are not enough. Urgent steps need to be taken up to complete the 
recruitment process. The Committee finds that the A ction Taken Notes submitted by the 
Government appears to be of routine nature and with out any determination for execution 

within a targeted time. The Committee once again em phasizes that the Department will have 
to make vigorous efforts to raise the required fund s for RGNIYD.  The Department could 
not give an exact amount of funds allocated at the RE stage as the budget proposals sent by 
the Department are yet to be accepted by the Ministry of Finance.

41. The Committee views with serious concern that t he main constraint as it was informed, 
being faced by the Department is that the State Gov ernments are not taking due interest in proper 
maintenance and operation of the Hostels.  The Stat e Governments do not sanction adequate funds 
for maintenance of Hostels, due to which a number o f the hostel buildings are in bad shape.  In 
fact, 16 Youth Hostel buildings are under unauthori zed occupation and are being utilized for 
purposes other that the purpose for which these wer e constructed. In a number of cases, the Hostel 
management Committees have either not been formed o r are non-functional.  These issues have 
been taken up with the State Governments.  The Comm ittee strongly recommends that the 
Department must take all appropriate steps to get 1 6 hostels vacated from unauthorized occupants 
and it is imperative upon the Department to take al l requisite steps on priority to resolve and get 
extraneous activities stopped from these hostels.  The Committee views it very seriously and 
would like to have a status report on this within a month.

 The matter is being followed up with State Governm ents for vacating 16 Hostels 
from unauthorized occupants. In fact, 2 out of 16 y outh Hostels, namely, Bhiwani in Haryana and 
Secunderabad in Telangana, have been got vacated fr om unauthorized occupants. The issue of 
unauthorised occupation of Youth Hostels also came up during the meeting of Central Policy 
Committee of Youth Hostel Scheme held on 11.7.2015.   The Minutes of the Meeting have been 
circulated to all State/UT Governments for appropri ate action.  The Nehru Yuva Kendra 
Sangathan has also been entrusted to inspect all th ese Hostels and submit Report to the 
Department, so that further necessary steps can be taken. 
 
Comments of the Committee 
 
 The Committee views it very seriously that the  rec ommendation of the Committee 
for submitting a status report on unauthorized occu pancy of Youth Hostels within a month 
have been overlooked by the Department.  Further th e Action Taken notes submitted by the 
Department in the end of month of September, 2015   appears to be perfunctory.  The result 
could not  be derived without a distinct execution of strategy and  the problem of 
unauthorized occupancy of Youth Hostels will contin ue ceaselessly. The Committee, 
henceforth,  notes with dismay that inadequacy of r eal spirit would fail to promptly resolve 
the issue of unauthorized occupancy of Youth Hostels. 
Recommendations/observations  
43. The Committee is also seized of the fact that the S tates have been demanding sanction of 
additional Hostels.  However, currently no new Host els are being set up.  The erstwhile Planning 
Commission (now NITI Ayog) had asked the Department  to explore PPP Model for operation of 
Hostels.  Accordingly, a Proposal was sent for 3 Ho stels seeking suggestions of the Commission, 

but no reply was received.  Some States are suggest ing that the Hostels should be either entirely 
with the Centre or the State and that the current m odel of joint management is not working well. 
 The Committee feels that all the suggestions and o ptions should be carefully considered in 
consultation with the Ministry of Finance and the N ITI Ayog, for deciding the future course of 
action and the Committee may be apprised of this position as well.  
 
Action Taken  
 
 In the meeting of the Central Policy Committee hel d on 11.07.2015, it was decided that the 
ownership of the Youth Hostels would remain with th e Government of India, Ministry of Youth 
Affairs and Sports and the existing system of joint management will continue.  
 
Comments of the Committee  
 
 Some States have suggested that the current model of joint management of Hostels is 
not working well, yet the Ministry of Youth Affairs  and Sports has decided to stick to this 
system. This is a matter of great concern. The Comm ittee is of the view that experts in this 
field should be consulted for the proper management  of the Hostels as Hostels are an 
important tool to promote youth travel and to enabl e young people to experience the rich 
cultural heritage of the country. Regarding the est ablishment of additional Hostels, the 
Committee feels that the Department should follow-up with NITI Ayog earnestly.

GOVERNMENT ARE STILL AWAITED 
 
DEMOGRAPHIC DIVIDEND

youth population in the country including adolescents is around 550 million with about 70 per cent 
being in rural areas.  This phenomenal rise in the youth population has made India the youngest

demographic dividend.  The Committee was informed t hat in India, youth in the age-group of 15-
29 years constitute 27.5% of the population.  It is  expected that by the year 2020, the population of

and as high as 48 years for Japan.  In a nutshell, this ‘demographic dividend’ offers a great 

opportunity and the skill development of youth must  be seen as a key priority by the Government.  
The Committee is of the opinion that such a demogra phic advantage would be wasted, if it is not 
accompanied by simultaneous process of creation of jobs and development of skills for these new 
work forces.

CONCLUSION  
 
Recommendations/observations 
 
68. The Committee feels that to revive sports culture, the government should revisit the 
sporting framework of India.  This is also the need  of the hour as India is reaping benefits of 
demographic dividend in the form of young populatio n which can easily be channelized to sports 
and games for achieving better results.  Otherwise,  achievement of goals by utilizing the available 
immense potential of the country in sports would be  difficult to realize.  For achieving improved 
performance in sports internationally the governmen t needs to play a proactive role in promoting 
sports in India to establish the country as a sport ing nation.  The Committee hopes that with 
improved sporting infrastructure and infusion of la test technology in training of sportspersons 
India would show better results at the next Olympics to be held at Rio in Brazil.     
 
Action Taken  
 
The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports is taking all possible steps for realization of twin 
objectives of National Sports Policy 2001 viz., mas s participation in sports and achieving 

excellence in sports. Apart from review and revisio n of existing Schemes and policies of the 
Ministry from time to time, the Department of Sport s has launched new schemes for achieving 
these two objectives of the National Sports Policy 2001.  
A new scheme, namely National Sports Talent Search Scheme (NSTSS) has been formulated for 
talent identification in the age group of 8-12 year s and nurturing of identified talented 
sportspersons with the objectives identification of  sporting talent among students in the age group 
of 8–12 years (for admission in Class IV to Class V I) who possess inborn qualities such as 
anthropometric, physical and physiological capabili ties without any anatomical infirmities and 
nurturing of the Sporting Potential / talent in Dis trict level Sports schools / Central Sports 
 Schools / National Sports Academies etc., to make them excel at the National and 
international sports competitions.  
2000 children (1000 boys and 1000 girls) who are fo und to be the best talented will be 
identified and admitted in the (a) National Sports Academies (b) State Sports Academies/Sports 
Hostels run by State Govts., (c) State Sports Schol arships, (d) State Sports Schools, (e) Central 
Sports Schools and (f) Sports Training Centre (STC) /Special Area Games (SAG) of Sports 
Authority of India (SAI).  
Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports and the Sports A uthority of India are geared up for 
preparation and training of sportspersons/teams for India’s improved performance at Rio Olympics 
2016.  
A programme, namely TOP (Target Olympic Podium) Scheme, has been formulated within 
the overall ambit of National Sports Development Fu nd (NSDF) with the objective of identifying 
and supporting potential medal prospects for 2016 a nd 2020 Olympic Games.  Focused disciplines 
will be Athletics, Archery, Badminton, Boxing, Wres tling, Weightlifting and Shooting.  The 
selected athletes will be provided financial assist ance for their customized training at Institutes 
having world class facilities and other necessary s upport.  Benchmark for selection of athletes 
under the scheme will be in relation to internation al standards.  There will be annual/semi-annual 
review of performance of selected athletes.    
Customized training at Institutes having world clas s facilities and other necessary support is being 
provided to the elite athletes, which would result in improved performance and a higher position in 
medals tally for the country in international sports events and mega-sports events.

BUDGETARY ALLOCATION 
 
Recommendations/observations  
11. The Committee notes with concern that there has bee n a gap between the projected 
demands and the actual allocated funds during all t hese years. The Committee, therefore, keeping 
in view the major emphasis of the Department during 2015-16 for preparation of sportspersons and 
teams for Rio Olympics 2016 feels that the Departme nt should endeavour to get enhancement of 
the fund at the RE stage so that the gap in allocat ion is set off appropriately.  The Committee also 
recommends that Ministry of Finance should release more funds for the Department so that lack of 
funds should not come in the way of our preparation  as well as performance at the next Olympics 
and initiatives to be taken by the Department also to tap non-governmental sources.

Funds for preparation and training of the Indian sp ortspersons and teams for Rio Olympics 
2016 need to be supplemented through more allocatio n under Scheme of Assistance to National 
Sports Federations (NSFs) and further allocation fo r corpus to  National Sports Development Fund 
(NSDF) for meeting the expenses of the sportsperson s and teams on training, both within the 
country and abroad and competition exposure. The Mi nistry plans to approach the Ministry of 
Finance for allocating additional funds under the Scheme of Assistance to NSFs.    
 
For augmenting the funds position of the NSDF, the Ministry has written to corporate 
entities, both in public and private sector also, to contribute generously to NSDF.  
 
Comments of the Committee 
 The Committee finds that there is need to focus for  the augmentation of matching 
contribution of Government of India in NSDF.  The c oncerted endeavours are required to be 

taken by the Department of Sports to get the matchi ng contribution of Government of India 
at par with the present level of contribution to NS DF by all other donors.  The impediments 
in achieving this target by the Department of Sport s are unacceptable to the Committee.  
Owing to the present initiatives taken by the Commi ttee it is felt that full blown efforts are 
needed by the Department of Sports to mobilise the contribution under Social Responsibility 
by PSBs/PSEs to National Sports Development Fund.  It is high time, that the augmentation 
of sports fund problem is tackled seriously and vig orous steps taken to remove the stumbling  
blocks which are likely to crop up. 
 
 
SPORTS AUTHORITY OF INDIA 
 
Recommendations/observations  
21.  The Committee was given to understand that in Andhr a Pradesh there is no dearth of sports 
talents in archery, particularly in interior tribal  areas.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that if 
the Budget allocation gets enhanced at the RE stage ,  the Department may consider developing an 
archery training centre for Andhra Pradesh so as to  tap the potential of exemplary talents that have 
been lying in the rural tribal areas who would contribute to the national sports talent.    
 
Action Taken 
 
Following bifurcation of the State of Andhra Prades h, most of the Sports Infrastructure has 
fallen in the newly created State of Telangana.  Th erefore, the State Government of Andhra Pradesh 
needs to approach SAI with proposals to develop new  SAI Centres in the State.  While SAI will 
consider their proposals, including setting up of T raining Centre for Tribals in Archery and other 
disciplines, under its Special Area games Scheme, a s per prescribed norms the State Government has 
to provide good infrastructure to SAI on long lease  which should include residential, administrative 
spaces as well as outdoor and indoor sports facilities. 
If suitable proposal is received from the State of Andhra Pradesh, SAI will seek necessary 
budget allocation (capital and recurring cost) and sanction of required manpower for opening of a 
centre from the Governing Body of SAI. 
 
Comments of the Committee  
 
It is sad to note that no initiatives have been tak en to establish any archery training 
centre in tribal areas of Andhra Pradesh. On one ha nd, SAI is waiting for the State 
Government to send its proposal, on the other hand, the State Government  approaching SAI 
for the said purpose is not within sight. Precious time and talents get wasted in the process. 
The Committee strongly feels that it becomes imperative on SAI to point out to the respective 
authorities of the State Government of Andhra Prade sh about the intricacies and 
conditionalities for assistance of the Department o f Sports for developing sports/ training 
centres  and consider establishing such centres so that maximum benefits can be reaped in 
time to come.  
 
ASSISTANCE TO NATIONAL SPORTS FEDERATIONS  
 
Recommendations/observations  

27.  The Committee finds it very disheartening on the is sue of non-compliance of the 
guidelines of the Department by the NSFs and recomm ends to evolve a suitable mechanism in this 
regard so that the preparation as well as participa tion of the sportspersons in important national 
and international events is not affected adversely. 
 
Action Taken 
 
NSFs are responsible and accountable for the overal l management, direction, control, 
regulation, promotion and development of the discip lines for which they are recognized by the 
concerned International Federations. They are expec ted to discharge these responsibilities in 
consonance with the principles laid down in the Oly mpic Charter or in the charter of the Indian 
Olympic Association or of the relevant Internationa l Federation as the case may be while being 
compliant with Government guidelines applicable to NSFs. In case of non-compliance, where any 
NSF has been suspended/de-recognised, the assistanc e as admissible is given to athletes to 
facilitate their participation in various events by  the Sports Authority of India.  National Sports 
Code is expected to provide for more specific guide lines to be followed by various sports 
federations. 
 
Comments of the Committee  
  
When National Sports Federations (NSFs) are suspend ed/derecognised on account of 
non-compliance of guidelines of the Department, it is the sportspersons who get affected the 
most. At a time when medal prospects in many intern ational events including Olympics, are 
increasing, it is unfortunate to know that these bo dies are not doing their part in promotion 
and development of sports. The extent to which the performance of sportspersons have been 
affected despite the assistance extended by SAI, th e Committee feels, is the looming spectre  
about which the information has not been provided.  The Committee would appreciate if 
concerted efforts are initiated to ensure that thes e problems are tackled earnestly and the 
excuses  for the fillip in the name of National Sports Code is unacceptable.  
 
URBAN SPORTS INFRASTRUCTURE 
 
Recommendations/observations 
 
35.  The Committee came to know that Rs.40 crores was al located for the purpose in BE 2014-
15 and it was reduced to Rs.25 crores in RE 2014-15 .  The Committee shows its concern that the 
reduction in RE was on account of non-receipt of Ut ilisation Certificates by the implementing 
agencies.  The actual expenditure is amounting to R s. 23.14 crores till February 2015.  The 
Committee finds this as a very good scheme which is  for providing sports infrastructure in urban

discouraging.  Rs. 40 crores BE is reduced to Rs. 2 5 crores RE and even that could not be utilized

in time so that the allocation pattern is not affected adversely in future. 
 
Action Taken 

 
In deference to the wishes of the Committee, it is proposed to take up the matter with the 
Chief Secretaries/ LGs of the States/UTs at the lev el of Secretary (Sports) to expedite the 
Utilization Certificates on priority so as to ensure release of further grants by the department under  
its various schemes. A list of defaulting States/UTs as on 28.05.2015 is attached as Annexure –II.

Non-submission of Utilisation Certificates by the i mplementing agencies seems to be a
